title: Cascade routing (FrugalGPT)
change: Opt-in PASTURE_CASCADE: answer local, escalate to cloud only on low confidence
reason: Committing to a route up front wastes cloud spend on prompts the local model could handle
effect: Verified: cascade never runs for sensitive content or streaming; cloud failure falls back to local. Tested with mock backends.
grounding: ADR-011; FrugalGPT arXiv:2305.05176

title: Data-driven threshold calibration
change: calibrate command recommends PASTURE_THRESHOLD from the user's own PII-free token-size log
reason: The strongest routers are learned from labels a single local user does not have; calibrate the one length knob from real usage instead
effect: Advisory threshold derived from the (1-target) quantile of logged prompt sizes; stays deterministic and offline
grounding: ADR-023, ADR-015; RouterBench arXiv:2403.12031, UCCI arXiv:2605.18796

title: Privacy-classification routing
change: std-only classifier forces sensitive prompts local, overriding even --cloud
reason: A privacy-first proxy's worst failure is leaking PII to the cloud
effect: Sensitive content kept on-device unless PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD; only category labels logged, never values
grounding: ADR-007; PRISM arXiv:2511.22788

title: Richer difficulty features
change: Hard-signal step adds reasoning-depth, strict-format, math-density, multi-question markers (EN+JA)
reason: Token length alone under-routes genuinely hard short prompts
effect: More hard prompts escalate to the stronger model; local-only setups unaffected; still deterministic and label-only
grounding: ADR-008; routing survey arXiv:2506.06579

title: Evaluation harness
change: eval runs a labelled set (correctness) + threshold sweep (cost/locality)
reason: Routing quality must be measured, not asserted, to answer the brittle-rules critique
effect: Accuracy, cloud rate, false/missed escalations reported; fully offline regression gate
grounding: ADR-012; RouterBench arXiv:2403.12031

title: Exact-match response cache
change: Opt-in PASTURE_CACHE keyed by hash(model+messages), bounded FIFO
reason: Repeated identical prompts should not re-pay the backend
effect: Hits skip the backend (cost 0, route=cache); sensitive prompts never cached; composes with cascade
grounding: ADR-013; GPTCache

title: SSE streaming
change: Proxy detects stream:true and streams chat.completion.chunk frames for all backends
reason: OpenAI clients expect token-by-token streaming
effect: Local NDJSON/SSE re-emitted over the std-only socket; privacy/routing decide before the first byte; cascade stays non-streaming by design

title: API-surface parity: /v1/models + /v1/embeddings
change: Added GET /v1/models and POST /v1/embeddings (local-only) to the proxy
reason: Many OpenAI clients probe /v1/models on connect and 404 hid the server; embeddings clients (LlamaIndex/LangChain) need the endpoint
effect: Clients connect cleanly; embeddings routed to the local backend only; OpenAI-shaped responses; unit-tested
grounding: ADR-030, ADR-034; COMPETITIVE.md peer-surface gap

title: Cloud retry + local fallback
change: Classify 5xx as retryable Transport; complete_with_retry with exponential backoff (PASTURE_CLOUD_RETRY), then fall back to local
reason: A single transient cloud error should not fail the request or silently degrade
effect: Transient failures retried then fall back to local when available; 4xx not retried; tested with a flaky mock (no sleeps)
grounding: ADR-032; LiteLLM/Portkey failover

title: Tool/function-calling as a hard signal
change: parse_request detects non-empty tools/functions; decide_full escalates to cloud
reason: Tool use is most reliable on the stronger model; unparsed tool calls were misroutable to a weak local model
effect: Tool requests escalate (gated by code_to_cloud, overridden by privacy); fields passed through unchanged; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-031

title: GPU-less / local-only PC enhancement
change: PASTURE_LOCAL_ONLY (force local), PASTURE_LOCAL_FAST_MODEL (dual-local routing), PASTURE_INJECT_CONTEXT (date/OS system message); CPU-only model tier in `models`
reason: No-GPU and air-gapped machines should run a capable local assistant with zero cloud dependency
effect: All traffic stays on-device when enabled; simple short prompts use a tiny fast model; lightweight models gain date/OS grounding; std-only
grounding: ADR-035; two-tier local cascade (RESEARCH.md cat.1/cat.8)

title: PII detection hardening (7 to 10 categories)
change: Added pem_key, url_credential, env_secret detectors; expanded EN/JA keywords and vendor key prefixes
reason: PEM private keys, DB URLs with credentials, and .env secret pastes were not caught and could leak to the cloud
effect: Three new leakage vectors detected before they leave the machine; labels only, never values; 26 new tests
grounding: ADR-036; over-classification bias (false positive=local=cheap, false negative=leak)

title: Self-improvement ledger
change: Machine-readable IMPROVEMENTS.jsonl (change/reason/effect/status/grounding) + `pasture improvements` + a CI-checked validator
reason: The improvement history was human prose scattered across three docs; the durable asset is a verified, queryable improvement record, not the model
effect: Every shipped change is now a structured, self-verifying causal record; the bundled ledger is validated by a compile-time test
grounding: ADR-037; RSI=Search*Verification*Compression — this is the Compression/asset layer

title: Optional semantic cache
change: Cosine-similarity cache via the local /v1/embeddings (off by default)
reason: Exact-match caching misses paraphrases; embeddings can catch them without a new crate
effect: Not yet implemented; would stay opt-in to preserve the zero-dependency default
grounding: COMPETITIVE.md IMP-12; GPTCache, arXiv:2603.03301

title: Calibrated-uncertainty escalation (UCCI-style)
change: Map local mean-logprob to an estimated error probability (isotonic, std-only)
reason: Turns the escalation knob from a target-rate into a target-accuracy budget
effect: Not yet implemented; honest about single-user label scarcity
grounding: COMPETITIVE.md IMP-13; UCCI arXiv:2605.18796

title: Bearer-token auth + rate-limit
change: Optional PASTURE_AUTH_TOKEN (Bearer required on /v1/*, constant-time compare) and PASTURE_RATE_LIMIT (global token bucket, req/min); /health exempt; warn when bound non-localhost without auth
reason: The proxy is localhost-only by default but users expose it (PASTURE_LISTEN_ADDR=0.0.0.0); network exposure needs an auth + flood gate
effect: Gated via check_gate before route dispatch; 401/429 with OpenAI envelope; std-only token bucket tested deterministically (no sleeps); 12 tests; off by default so the zero-config single-user path is unchanged
grounding: ADR-040; COMPETITIVE.md IMP-15; LiteLLM/Portkey auth

title: Live metrics endpoint
change: GET /v1/stats returns JSON aggregates (route counts, rates, tokens, spend) over the cost-log counters
reason: A live observability view should not require parsing JSONL by hand; stats was CLI-only
effect: Read-only PII-free endpoint reusing cost::summarize; missing log reads as zeros; 4 tests (shape, empty, counted, roundtrip)
grounding: ADR-038, COMPETITIVE.md IMP-16; LiteLLM/Portkey dashboards

title: Sampling-parameter passthrough
change: parse_request extracts temperature/top_p/max_tokens/stop/seed/presence_penalty/frequency_penalty into SamplingParams; each backend serializes them (OpenAI fields, Ollama options/num_predict, Anthropic max_tokens+stop_sequences); cache key includes them
reason: Peers (LiteLLM/OpenRouter/Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM) honor these; Pasture silently dropped them, so temperature:0 determinism and max_tokens cost caps were ignored — a correctness gap
effect: Client sampling intent now reaches the backend; cache no longer serves a temperature:0 answer to a temperature:1 request; non-finite values rejected at parse; 11 tests across parse/build/cache
grounding: ADR-039; OpenAI Chat Completions API; peer-gateway parity

title: CORS / OPTIONS preflight for browser clients
change: Opt-in PASTURE_CORS_ORIGINS (comma list or *): OPTIONS preflight answered with 204 + Access-Control-Allow-* (before auth), and Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflected on all responses incl. SSE; specific origins add Vary: Origin
reason: Browser UIs (Open WebUI web, custom dashboards) cannot call the proxy without CORS preflight handling — peers (Ollama/LM Studio/LiteLLM) all support it
effect: Browser clients can connect when enabled; off by default since a localhost server with * CORS is reachable by any visited website; deterministic, std-only; 8 tests (parse/match/headers/preflight/roundtrip)
grounding: ADR-041; Ollama OLLAMA_ORIGINS, LM Studio/LiteLLM CORS

title: Streaming token usage (stream_options.include_usage)
change: When the client sets stream_options.include_usage, the SSE stream emits a final chunk with empty choices and a usage object (prompt/completion/total_tokens) before [DONE]
reason: OpenAI/LiteLLM/vLLM emit usage on the stream when asked; Pasture's streaming path reported no token counts, so clients tracking cost/length on streamed responses got nothing
effect: Streamed responses now carry usage when requested; off unless the client opts in (no extra bytes otherwise); std-only; 4 tests (parse/build/roundtrip with and without)
grounding: ADR-042; OpenAI Chat Completions streaming usage

title: Structured-output (response_format / JSON mode) passthrough
change: parse_request captures response_format; forwarded verbatim to OpenAI/OpenAI-compat and translated for Ollama (json_object -> format:json, json_schema -> the schema in top-level format); cache key includes it. Added a JsonValue serializer (to_json_string) to round-trip arbitrary values
reason: OpenAI/vLLM/LM Studio/Ollama all support JSON mode / structured outputs; Pasture silently dropped response_format, so JSON-mode requests returned free-form text
effect: JSON-mode and json_schema requests now reach the backend; deterministic BTreeMap-ordered serializer reused for hashing; 9 tests (serializer round-trip, per-backend emission, parse, cache)
grounding: ADR-043; OpenAI response_format, Ollama format

title: Unique completion ids (chatcmpl-...)
change: Responses now carry a unique id (chatcmpl-<clock><counter>) instead of the constant "pasture"; streaming chunks share one id per stream (id threaded through build_openai_chunk / build_openai_usage_chunk)
reason: OpenAI returns a unique id per completion that logging/observability/dedup tooling keys on; a constant id breaks tracing and de-duplication
effect: Buffered responses get a fresh id each; all chunks of one stream share it; uniqueness via an atomic counter; std-only; 2 new tests (uniqueness, stream id-consistency) + builder call-site updates
grounding: ADR-044; OpenAI chat.completion id

title: GET /v1/models/{id} (single model retrieve)
change: Added the OpenAI models.retrieve endpoint: /v1/models/{id} returns the model object when id is configured, else 404; the bare /v1/models list path is unaffected
reason: OpenAI SDK and some client validation flows call models.retrieve(id); Pasture only served the list, so retrieve fell through to the list via starts_with
effect: Single-model GET returns OpenAI {id,object:model,owned_by} or a 404 envelope; query string and trailing slash tolerated; 5 tests
grounding: ADR-045; OpenAI Models API

title: Per-connection socket read/write timeout (slow-loris guard)
change: serve sets a per-connection read+write timeout (PASTURE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, default 30s); read_request maps a timed-out read to a 408 response instead of pinning the worker; 0 disables
reason: read_request had no timeout, so a slow/dead client could hold a bounded worker thread forever and a handful could exhaust the pool (slow-loris DoS)
effect: Slow clients are dropped with 408 after the window, freeing the worker; std-only TcpStream timeouts; 408 added to the status table; 3 tests incl. a fast 50ms timeout roundtrip
grounding: ADR-046; continuation of IMP-21 DoS hardening (body/header/recursion caps)

title: system_fingerprint on responses and stream chunks
change: All buffered chat responses and SSE chunks now carry system_fingerprint: fp_pasture_XXXXXXXX (FNV-1a of model name, truncated to 32 bits); all chunks of one stream share the fingerprint computed at stream start
reason: OpenAI clients key caching-invalidation, dedup, and model-change detection on system_fingerprint; Pasture omitted it entirely, breaking those clients
effect: Deterministic, model-keyed fingerprint on every response and chunk; same-stream consistency; std-only FNV hash, no I/O; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-047; OpenAI Chat Completions API system_fingerprint

title: model field in streaming chunks
change: build_openai_chunk and build_openai_usage_chunk now carry a model field; the streaming path passes req.model computed once at stream start
reason: OpenAI includes model in every chat.completion.chunk; clients logging or displaying per-chunk model received nothing
effect: All SSE chunks carry model; same-stream consistency; std-only; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-048; OpenAI Chat Completions streaming API

title: logprobs:null in choice objects
change: build_openai_response and build_openai_chunk now emit logprobs:null in each choice object (usage chunk unaffected, empty choices)
reason: OpenAI always includes a logprobs key in each choice; strict client schema validators could reject Pasture responses that omitted it
effect: Buffered and streaming choices carry logprobs:null, completing choice-object parity; purely additive, std-only; 2 tests
grounding: ADR-049; OpenAI Chat Completions choice object

title: HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connection reuse
change: handle_connection loops (cap 100) serving sequential requests on one TCP connection; per-connection conn_buf carries read-ahead bytes across iterations; write_response gains keep_alive:bool for Connection header; HTTP/1.1 defaults to keep-alive, HTTP/1.0 to close, SSE always closes
reason: Re-connecting for every request adds one TCP round-trip of latency; OpenAI clients and proxies expect persistent connections for batch workloads
effect: Clients reuse connections; read-ahead bytes preserved correctly via drain; existing timeout/body-cap/rate-limit guards apply per-request; std-only; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-050; HTTP/1.1 RFC 7230 §6.3; LiteLLM/OpenRouter persistent connection behaviour

title: HEAD /health and /v1/engines alias
change: HEAD /health accepted (correct Content-Length, no body, RFC 7231); /v1/engines[/{id}] aliased to /v1/models in dispatch; write_head_response helper
reason: Monitoring tools use HEAD for liveness probes; old OpenAI SDK versions and some clients probe /v1/engines for model discovery
effect: HEAD liveness checks work; old SDK clients discover models without 404; purely additive, std-only; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-051; RFC 7231 §4.3.2; OpenAI engines API (deprecated)

title: X-Request-ID echo
change: read_request parses X-Request-ID header (CRLF-injection guard strips \r\n from value); handle_connection echoes it back on every response via extra header block; SSE responses also carry the echoed header; absent when client omits the header
reason: Clients correlate asynchronous responses and trace distributed calls by request ID; without echo the ID is invisible to the caller
effect: All response types (buffered, streaming, error, HEAD) echo the caller-supplied ID; CRLF injection guarded; purely additive, std-only; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-052; OpenAI API X-Request-ID convention; LiteLLM request-id passthrough

title: 405 Method Not Allowed for known routes
change: route_allowed_methods maps known paths to their allowed methods; dispatch catch-all returns 405 + Allow header when the path is known but the method is wrong, 404 only for unknown paths
reason: HTTP/1.1 RFC 7231 §6.5.5 requires 405 with an Allow header when the method is not supported; returning 404 for wrong methods misleads clients and debuggers
effect: GET /v1/chat/completions → 405 Allow: POST,OPTIONS; DELETE /v1/models → 405; /no/such → 404; purely additive, std-only; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-053; RFC 7231 §6.5.5; LiteLLM/OpenRouter correct method handling

title: tool_choice as a hard escalation signal
change: parse_request also sets has_tools=true when tool_choice is present and not "none" (covers auto/required/named-function values)
reason: Some clients send tool_choice without a tools array, or send tool_choice:required which is stronger than auto; both are unambiguous intents to call a tool
effect: tool_choice:auto/required/named-function all escalate to the stronger model; tool_choice:none does not; combines with existing tools/functions detection; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-054; OpenAI tool_choice parameter spec; SPEC.md §3.1 deferred item

title: POST /v1/completions legacy text-completion shim
change: parse_legacy_completion maps prompt (string or string array) to a single user message; handle_legacy_completion routes through run_completion and formats the result as object:text_completion with choices[].text; id prefix cmpl- matches OpenAI convention; 405 for wrong method; streaming not supported via this shim
reason: Many older LLM clients, SDKs, and tools (LM Studio, older langchain/openai-python) default to /v1/completions; returning 404 breaks those clients silently
effect: Old-style text-completion clients work without reconfiguration; prompts are routed through the same privacy/routing/cache pipeline; std-only, 6 tests
grounding: ADR-055; OpenAI text completions API (deprecated but widely used); LiteLLM completions compat

title: Configurable system prompt via PASTURE_SYSTEM_PROMPT
change: system_prompt: Option<String> field on Proxy; with_system_prompt builder; prepend_system_prompt helper merges with existing system messages; applied first in run_completion (before inject_context); PASTURE_SYSTEM_PROMPT env var and system_prompt config-file key; empty string treated as None
reason: Single-user PC assistant use case requires a persistent persona/instruction prompt (e.g. "You are a coding assistant") without rebuilding inject_context; complementary to date/OS injection
effect: All requests get the configured system prompt prepended; existing system messages in the request are merged (configured prompt first); std-only, zero-dep; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-056; LiteLLM system_prompt global override; Ollama modelfile system parameter

title: Live cache hit/miss counters in /v1/stats
change: AtomicU64 hits/misses added to ResponseCache; get() increments on hit or miss; hits()/misses() accessors; handle_stats reads live counters from self.cache; build_stats_response gains cache_hits/cache_misses params; 2 new fields in JSON response
reason: The existing cache_rate metric derives from the cost log (written only after completion); live counters show real-time effectiveness independent of log state, enabling tuning without log parsing
effect: GET /v1/stats now reports live cache_hits and cache_misses counts; std-only (AtomicU64); 2 new cache.rs tests + 1 stats integration test
grounding: ADR-057; Prometheus-style counters pattern; LiteLLM cache hit stats

title: 415 Unsupported Media Type for non-JSON POST bodies
change: read_request parses Content-Type header (lowercased); handle_connection checks it for POST requests before dispatch; returns 415 when Content-Type is present and does not start with application/json; absent Content-Type accepted (bare curl compatibility)
reason: Clients sending form-encoded or text bodies get a descriptive 415 instead of a confusing 400 JSON parse error; absent Content-Type accepted for simple HTTP clients
effect: Wrong Content-Type on POST → 415 with message; missing Content-Type → unchanged; charset suffixes accepted; std-only; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-058; RFC 7231 §6.5.13; OpenAI API Content-Type requirement

title: Model-pinned routing via req.model field
change: classify_and_decide checks req.model against configured local/cloud model names and the sentinels "local"/"cloud"; matching routes are forced via decide_full(forced=Some(Route)); with_model_names builder; wired in cli.rs from config.local_model/cloud_model
reason: Clients that are model-aware (e.g. specify model:gpt-4o-mini) expect to reach the cloud backend; without pinning they could be routed local on short prompts even when they explicitly requested a cloud model
effect: model:"local" / model:"<local_model_name>" → forced Local; model:"cloud" / model:"<cloud_model_name>" → forced Cloud (still subject to privacy override); unrecognised model names use normal routing; 5 tests
grounding: ADR-059; LiteLLM model routing; OpenRouter model-specific routing

title: Reject n > 1 with 400 Bad Request
change: parse_request checks the n field; if n != 1 (present and > 1 or zero), returns ProxyError::BadRequest with a clear message; n=1 and absent n both pass
reason: Without validation Pasture silently returns 1 completion when n>1 was requested, violating the contract; a clear 400 with explanation is always better than silent truncation
effect: Clients requesting n>1 get an immediate 400 with 'n must be 1' message; n=1 and absent n unchanged; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-060; OpenAI completions n parameter spec

title: POST /v1/moderations stub
change: handle_moderations parses input; build_moderations_response returns all categories false/0 in OpenAI moderation format; dispatch arm + 405 for wrong method
reason: Many OpenAI SDK versions call /v1/moderations unconditionally before or after completions; returning 404 breaks those clients silently
effect: Moderation clients receive a well-formed all-safe response and continue; Pasture does not run real content moderation (stub is explicit); std-only; 2 tests
grounding: ADR-061; OpenAI Moderations API; LiteLLM moderation passthrough

title: cache_size and cache_capacity in /v1/stats
change: ResponseCache gains cap() accessor; handle_stats reads len()+cap() from the cache; build_stats_response gains cache_size/cache_capacity params; both added to the JSON response
reason: Operators need to know whether the cache is near capacity to tune PASTURE_CACHE; the hit rate alone is insufficient for sizing decisions
effect: GET /v1/stats now includes cache_size (current entries) and cache_capacity (max entries); 0 when cache is disabled; std-only; 2 tests
grounding: ADR-062; Prometheus gauge naming conventions

title: Prometheus /metrics endpoint
change: build_metrics_response emits Prometheus text format v0.0.4 for all routing counters, cache stats, and token/cost gauges; handle_metrics reads the cost log + live cache state; write_plain_response sends text/plain; version=0.0.4; /metrics added to route_allowed_methods and dispatch; ADR-063
reason: Operators need a live pull-based metrics endpoint compatible with Prometheus/Grafana without parsing JSONL logs; /v1/stats is human-readable JSON but not scrape-compatible
effect: GET /metrics returns HELP/TYPE headers and labelled counters (route=local/cloud/cache) plus token/cost/cache gauges; wrong method returns 405; std-only; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-063; Prometheus exposition format v0.0.4; LiteLLM /metrics; Portkey observability

title: X-Response-Time header on every response
change: handle_connection captures Instant::now() after request parsing; te() closure appends X-Response-Time: <N>ms header to every write_response/write_plain_response/write_head_response/write_sse_headers call; covers success, error, and SSE paths (SSE reflects time-to-first-byte)
reason: Operators and SDK clients need per-request latency without parsing JSONL logs; X-Response-Time is a de-facto standard header used by nginx, Fastly, and Heroku
effect: Every HTTP response now carries X-Response-Time: <N>ms; std-only (std::time::Instant); backward-compatible (additive header); 3 tests
grounding: ADR-064; nginx X-Response-Time; Fastly / Heroku latency header conventions

title: Version field in /health response + 501 stubs for /v1/audio and /v1/images
change: /health response now includes version (compile-time CARGO_PKG_VERSION via concat!/env!); 501 Not Implemented returned for POST /v1/audio/* and /v1/images/* with not_supported error type; route_allowed_methods covers these paths so wrong-method returns 405 not 404; 501 and 405/415 added to status reason table in write_response
reason: Clients detect mismatched Pasture versions via /health; 404 for audio/images endpoints misleads SDK clients that probe them unconditionally — 501 correctly signals recognised-but-unsupported
effect: /health body includes version:"0.26.0"; audio/images return 501; wrong method still returns 405; status reason table more complete; std-only; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-065; OpenAI SDK multi-endpoint probing; nginx/LiteLLM health check version convention

title: Structured per-request access log (JSONL, no PII)
change: access_log: Option<String> field on Proxy; with_access_log builder; append_access_log writes one JSONL line per request (ts/method/path/status/ms/request_id?) before each response via access_log! macro; wr!/wrp!/wrh! macros unify response-writing in handle_connection; PASTURE_ACCESS_LOG env var + access_log config key; wired in cli.rs
reason: Operators need per-request visibility (latency, status, path) without parsing JSONL cost logs or scraping /metrics; access logs are the standard observability primitive
effect: PASTURE_ACCESS_LOG=/path enables append-only JSONL with ts/method/path/status/ms and optional request_id; no prompt content, no auth tokens, no PII; off by default; std-only; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-066; nginx/LiteLLM/Portkey access log conventions; OpenTelemetry access-log semantic conventions

title: TTL (time-to-live) eviction for the response cache
change: ResponseCache stores (CompletionResponse, Instant) pairs; get() changed to &mut self to lazily evict expired entries (removes from map, counts as miss); with_max_age builder + set_max_age mutating method; with_cache_ttl Proxy builder; PASTURE_CACHE_TTL env var (seconds, 0=disabled) + cache_ttl_secs config key; wired in cli.rs
reason: Without TTL, stale cached responses (outdated facts, old code, revoked context) are served indefinitely; long-running proxy processes need time-bounded cache entries for correctness
effect: PASTURE_CACHE_TTL=3600 makes entries expire after 1 hour; expired entries removed on first get after expiry; len() stays accurate; off by default (0=no TTL); std-only; 4 cache tests
grounding: ADR-067; Redis TTL semantics; GPTCache TTL; Nginx proxy_cache_valid

title: Cache key whitespace normalisation
change: request_key() trims leading/trailing whitespace from message content before hashing (m.content.trim()); internal whitespace left intact; adds 1 test
reason: Trailing spaces and leading spaces from copy-paste or SDK padding produce cache misses for semantically identical requests
effect: Prompts that differ only in leading/trailing whitespace now share a cache key; zero runtime cost (no allocation — str::trim returns a slice); backward-compatible; 1 test
grounding: ADR-068; COMPETITIVE.md IMP-11 cache-key normalisation

title: RouterBench-format external eval loader
change: OwnedEvalCase (heap prompt) + run_eval_owned + load_eval_cases(path) parse a JSONL file ({"prompt":"...","expected":"local"|"cloud"}); pasture eval --external <file> CLI option; blank lines and // comments skipped; 5 tests
reason: The built-in 18-case eval set is the offline regression gate; users need to validate routing on their own labelled prompts or a public benchmark (RouterBench) without adding a dependency
effect: pasture eval --external cases.jsonl runs any labelled JSONL set through the same routing pipeline (privacy + routing + sensitivity); missing file / bad format return a clear error message; JSONL format matches the project's existing log conventions; std-only (BufRead + crate::json::parse); 5 tests
grounding: ADR-069; COMPETITIVE.md IMP-17; RouterBench arXiv:2403.12031; routing survey arXiv:2603.04445

title: More reasoning/format hard-signal markers (eval-safe)
change: Added strong, specific markers to REASONING_MARKERS (chain-of-thought, show your work, show your reasoning, walk me through, 理由を説明) and FORMAT_MARKERS (as xml, csv format, write a test, unit test, shell script, bash script, dockerfile, 単体テスト); 1 test
reason: Genuinely hard short prompts (e.g. 'write a unit test for foo', 'walk me through the proof') were under-routed to the weak local model because they fell below the length threshold and matched no existing marker — the same under-routing IMP-4 set out to fix
effect: These task-specific prompts now escalate to the stronger model; markers are specific enough to avoid broad false escalations; verified eval-safe — the curated 18-case regression still scores 100% (no Local case matches a new marker); std-only; 1 test
grounding: ADR-081; routing survey arXiv:2506.06579; continuation of IMP-4 richer difficulty features

title: Machine-readable --json output for eval and stats
change: EvalReport::to_json(threshold) and CostSummary::to_json() build compact JSON (validated by round-tripping through the in-tree parser); pasture eval --json and pasture stats --json print it and return; stats --json emits zeros (valid JSON) even with an empty log; USAGE updated; 4 tests
reason: eval/stats were human-text only, so CI pipelines and dashboards had to scrape prose to gate on routing accuracy or cloud spend; peers (LiteLLM) expose structured metrics for exactly this
effect: pasture eval --json yields {total,correct,accuracy,cloud_rate,false/missed_escalations,threshold}; pasture stats --json yields the cost aggregates; both are valid JSON consumable by CI/jq; human output unchanged without the flag; std-only; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-080; machine-readable CLI convention; LiteLLM structured metrics; CI gating use case

title: Parse UTF-16 surrogate-pair \u escapes (emoji)
change: parse_unicode_escape returns the raw u32 code unit; parse_string combines a high surrogate (D800-DBFF) with a following low surrogate (DC00-DFFF) into the real code point (0x10000 + ((hi-D800)<<10) + (lo-DC00)); lone/mismatched surrogates error cleanly; 2 tests
reason: Python json.dumps defaults to ensure_ascii=True, which encodes non-BMP characters (emoji, CJK ext) as surrogate-pair escapes like \uD83D\uDE00; the old parser rejected these with 'invalid unicode code point', so any Python client sending an emoji via default json.dumps got a 400
effect: Requests containing surrogate-pair-escaped characters now parse correctly into the right Unicode scalar; literal UTF-8 emoji still works; lone surrogates rejected; std-only; 2 tests
grounding: ADR-077; RFC 8259 §7 (UTF-16 surrogate escapes); Python json.dumps ensure_ascii default

title: Ignore non-finite values in cost/logprob aggregation

title: Count emoji as dense tokens in estimate_tokens

The fix is conservative (1 token/char, the same as CJK); over-estimating is safer than under-estimating for routing quality

title: Guard format_cost/format_logprob against non-finite values
change: cost.rs: format_cost and format_logprob now return "0" when the input is non-finite (inf/NaN) before attempting format!; 3 new tests (format_cost_non_finite_is_zero, format_logprob_non_finite_is_zero, to_jsonl_non_finite_cost_is_valid_json)

A CostRecord with a non-finite cost_usd or logprob (propagated from a cloud backend bug or corrupt log replay) would therefore write an invalid JSONL line, silently corrupting the cost log. The corrupted line cannot be parsed by parse_log_line (the JSON parser correctly rejects inf/NaN literals), creating a silent data loss. The root cause is an upstream bug (ADR-078 fixed the aggregation path; this closes the serialisation path).
effect: to_jsonl always produces valid JSON regardless of upstream non-finite values; the JSONL log is never corrupted; 3 tests pass; cargo test: all tests pass, zero warnings; the fix is complementary to ADR-078 (which guards the read/aggregate path); std-only
grounding: ADR-091; ADR-078 (cost-finite-guard); JSON spec RFC 8259 §6 (disallows Infinity and NaN literals); Rust std fmt behaviour for f64::INFINITY/.NAN
risk: Low

title: Add Slack xapp- and HuggingFace hf_ token prefixes to PII classifier
change: privacy.rs KEY_PREFIXES: added "xapp-" (Slack App-Level Token, Socket Mode) and "hf_" (HuggingFace user/org/fine-grained access tokens); 1 new test (test_api_key_slack_xapp_and_huggingface) covering detection and length-threshold negatives for both prefixes; existing 45 privacy tests unaffected

HuggingFace hf_ tokens grant read/write access to model repos and private datasets — extremely common in LLM workflows and frequently pasted into prompts. Both would be sent to the cloud backend undetected, violating the privacy-first policy. The over-classification bias is intentional: a false positive keeps a prompt local; a false negative leaks credentials.

title: Boolean env vars now require truthy value instead of mere presence

For PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD this is a security regression: a user or deployment script setting PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD=false or PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD=0 intending to DISABLE cloud routing of sensitive content instead ENABLES it — silently routing PII/credentials to the cloud. The same issue affects NO_NUDGE, CASCADE, LOCAL_ONLY, INJECT_CONTEXT. The apply() config-file path already uses the correct matches!(val, "1"|"true"|"yes") form; the env var path was inconsistent.

grounding: ADR-093; ADR-007 privacy-first invariant I2/I3; PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD security contract; config-file apply() boolean precedent (ADR-076)

title: Trim PASTURE_AUTH_TOKEN env var before storing to fix auth failures
change: config.rs with_env(): PASTURE_AUTH_TOKEN now stores v.trim().to_string() instead of the raw value; 1 test (test_auth_token_config_strips_whitespace)
reason: A token set via PASTURE_AUTH_TOKEN=$(cat ~/.token) or with a trailing newline in a .env file was stored with the whitespace. auth_ok() in proxy.rs trims the client's bearer token from the Authorization header, but compares against the stored expected value — which is untrimmed. constant_time_eq returns false on the length mismatch, rejecting ALL valid auth requests with 401. Same root cause as ADR-082 (API key trim). The config-file path was already safe because apply() receives a pre-trimmed val.
effect: Tokens set via env var with trailing newlines (the most common shell-substitution pattern) now authenticate correctly; auth is not bypassed — a wrong token is still rejected; 444 tests pass; zero warnings; std-only
grounding: ADR-094; ADR-082 api-key-trim (same root cause: trim before store vs trim before compare); constant_time_eq in proxy.rs; HTTP Authorization Bearer spec

title: Add write timeout to http_post and http_post_streaming
change: backend.rs: set_write_timeout(Some(timeout)) added immediately after set_read_timeout in both http_post and http_post_streaming; uses the same configurable timeout duration (PASTURE_LOCAL_TIMEOUT, default 120s); no tests needed (the write path is not unit-testable without a slow mock server)
reason: http_post and http_post_streaming set a read timeout (to bound inference latency) but not a write timeout. If the local backend's kernel socket receive buffer fills — possible when sending a very large prompt to a heavily loaded backend — write_all blocks indefinitely. The proxy worker thread and the bounded thread pool slot are pinned until OS memory pressure eventually closes the socket. The write timeout ensures a stuck send is bounded to the same duration as a stuck receive, and the error is returned as BackendError::Transport (retryable if configured). Defensive: write blocking is rare on localhost but the protection is free.
effect: A stuck write_all now times out after PASTURE_LOCAL_TIMEOUT seconds instead of blocking indefinitely; no behaviour change for the normal (fast) write path; zero new tests (no observable output change, and simulating a slow socket receive buffer in unit tests would require OS-level mocking); 444 tests pass; zero warnings; std-only
grounding: ADR-095; ADR-084 configurable local timeout (same timeout reused); std::net::TcpStream::set_write_timeout docs
risk: Low

title: Escape method and path in access log to prevent JSON injection
change: proxy.rs append_access_log: method and norm_path are now wrapped with escape_string() before interpolation into the JSONL format string; 1 new test (test_access_log_escapes_method_and_path) verifies that JSON-breaking characters (quotes, backslashes) in the method/path are escaped and the resulting line is valid JSON
reason: method and norm_path come from the HTTP request line (user-supplied). Direct interpolation into the JSON format string without escaping allows a malicious client to inject arbitrary JSON by including quotes, backslashes, or newlines in the request method or path (e.g., GET"/evil" or /path"injected":1,"x). This corrupts the access log JSONL file, making records unparseable for downstream log consumers. The request_id field was already correctly escaped with escape_string(); the fix brings method and path to the same standard.
effect: Access log JSONL records are always valid JSON regardless of what the client sends in the request line; hostile characters are serialised as JSON escape sequences (\" etc.) preserving the original value; 1 test; 445 tests pass; zero warnings; std-only
grounding: ADR-096; OWASP Log Injection (A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures); escape_string() usage in proxy.rs build_error_response and other log paths; access log format contract
risk: High

title: Add header line count limit to read_request to prevent header-flood DoS
change: proxy.rs read_request: header parsing loop now uses enumerate(); on the 1001st header line it returns ReadOutcome::Closed immediately, refusing the request; 1 new test (test_excessive_header_count_closes_connection) verifies the connection is dropped silently with no response bytes
reason: The header parsing loop at proxy.rs:1938 iterated over all lines without a count bound. While the 1 MiB total header cap (line 1918) limits total bytes, a crafted request with 1 MiB of minimal 2-byte \r\n sequences generates ~500k loop iterations — each invoking to_ascii_lowercase() and multiple starts_with() checks. This is a CPU-bound micro-DoS: a single malicious connection can peg a worker thread for milliseconds per request. Defence-in-depth: a 1000-line cap (far above any legitimate request) stops the flood at the counting branch, consistent with ADR-026 (recursion depth cap) and the 1 MiB size guard.
effect: Requests with > 1000 header fields are silently closed (ReadOutcome::Closed); legitimate requests are unaffected (even verbose reverse-proxy chains rarely exceed 40 headers); 1 test; 446 tests pass; zero warnings; std-only
grounding: ADR-097; ADR-026 recursion depth cap (same defence-in-depth pattern); RFC 7230 §3.2 (no hard header-count limit — implementation choice); OWASP HTTP Header Injection
risk: Low

title: Remove TTL-expired entries from the FIFO order deque in cache.get()
change: cache.rs ResponseCache::get(): after removing a TTL-expired key from self.map, now also calls self.order.retain(|&k| k != key) to remove the ghost entry from the FIFO deque; 1 new test (test_ttl_expiry_removes_ghost_from_order_deque) verifies the deque is empty after expiring all entries and that FIFO eviction still works correctly afterwards
reason: When get() found a TTL-expired entry it removed it from self.map but not from self.order (the FIFO VecDeque). The ghost key remained in the deque permanently. With a TTL-enabled cache under repeated churn, the deque accumulated one entry per expired get() indefinitely — the map stays bounded at cap, but order grows without bound, causing a memory leak proportional to the number of TTL-expired gets since startup. The FIFO eviction path in put() tolerates ghost entries (map.remove on a missing key is a no-op), so the map invariant was preserved, but the deque was not bounded. For a typical deployment (cap=512, TTL=3600) with ~1 req/s, the deque would accumulate ~3.6k ghost entries per hour, ~87k/day.
effect: The FIFO order deque is now bounded by cap (same as the map); TTL-expired gets no longer leak memory; FIFO eviction continues to work correctly for non-expired entries; retain() is O(n) but only executed on TTL-expired cache misses (rare relative to hits); 1 test; 447 tests pass; zero warnings; std-only
grounding: ADR-098; VecDeque::retain docs; cache TTL design (IMP-cache-ttl in IMPROVEMENTS.jsonl); LRU/FIFO eviction invariants
risk: Low

title: Strip surrounding punctuation in looks_like_api_key so quoted credentials are detected
change: privacy.rs looks_like_api_key(): the token now has surrounding JSON/prose delimiters (double/single quote, comma, semicolon, parens, brackets, braces, backtick, angle brackets) trimmed via trim_matches before the prefix+length check; - and _ are deliberately preserved because they are valid inside prefixes (ghp_, glpat-, xoxb-); 1 new test (test_api_key_with_surrounding_punctuation) covers quoted/parenthesized/backticked forms and a no-false-positive case
reason: looks_like_api_key checked token.starts_with(prefix) on the raw whitespace-split token. A credential quoted in prose or code — the common real form, e.g. my key is "sk-..." or (sk-...) — has a leading quote/paren so starts_with("sk-") is false and the token is NOT classified as sensitive. The prompt would then be eligible for cloud routing, leaking the credential. looks_like_jwt already strips surrounding quotes/commas/semicolons for exactly this reason; this brings api-key detection to the same standard. title: Streaming pseudonymization parity (IMP-19 fix, ADR-137)
change: pseudonymize.rs: added StreamRestorer { mapping, pending } with push(delta)->String and finish()->String — buffers a trailing unterminated '<…' fragment so a token split across SSE deltas is never flushed partial and no held tail is dropped; restore() reused for the flushable portion. proxy.rs stream_chat_to_socket(): when pseudonymize && route==Cloud, pseudonymize req.messages before backend.stream_complete (masking the request) and feed each delta through StreamRestorer (restoring the response), flushing the restorer tail before the stop chunk. pseudonymize.rs: 5 StreamRestorer unit tests (single-delta token, split-across-deltas, literal '<' flushed at end, passthrough without mapping, byte-by-byte never-leaks). proxy_tests.rs: RecordingEchoBackend + 2 integration tests (streaming masks PII before cloud and restores in output; control: without pseudonymize raw text is sent).
reason: Socratic review of IMP-19 (ADR-132): pseudonymization was wired into run_completion (buffered) but NOT stream_chat_to_socket (streaming). With PASTURE_PSEUDONYMIZE=1 AND PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD set — the exact mode IMP-19 exists for — a stream:true cloud request sent raw PII (email/IPv4/phone/API-key) to the provider, silently breaking the feature's documented guarantee. The non-stream path masked; the stream path did not. Restoration in a stream is non-trivial: a token like <EMAIL_1> can split across two deltas, so a naive per-delta restore would miss the boundary; StreamRestorer holds the unterminated fragment until the token completes.
effect: 549 tests pass (7 new: 5 StreamRestorer + 2 proxy integration); clippy clean; zero new deps; no behaviour change when pseudonymize off or route!=Cloud; streaming now matches buffered path exactly
grounding: ADR-137; ADR-132 (IMP-19); privacy invariant I5; COMPETITIVE.md IMP-19
risk: Low — closes a privacy hole; opt-in feature; response restore adds at most one buffered '<…' fragment of latency and only when a '<' appears in output

title: Budget/spike guard on the streaming path (IMP-26 fix, ADR-138)
change: proxy.rs: extracted apply_budget_guard(req, route)->Result<Route,ProxyError> from the inline block in run_completion — returns the possibly-downgraded route (local-only action) or Err(BudgetExceeded) (block action, 429), no-op for non-cloud routes or when neither guard is configured. run_completion now calls it (behaviour-preserving). stream_chat_to_socket now calls it after classify_and_decide and before backend_for, threading the guarded `route` through backend selection, route_label, and the pseudonymize check. proxy_tests.rs: 3 streaming tests (block->429 before stream starts, local-only->redirect to local chunk, control: ample budget streams from cloud).
reason: Socratic review (continuing ADR-137's line): the IMP-26 budget/spike guard lived only in run_completion (buffered), not stream_chat_to_socket. A stream:true cloud request ran classify_and_decide -> backend_for and never checked the daily token cap or spike redirect, so PASTURE_BUDGET_DAILY_TOKENS and PASTURE_SPIKE_FACTOR were silently bypassed for streaming. Most chat UIs stream by default, so the spend cap a user set to control cost was trivially evaded. Streaming cloud completions already fed the counters via log_cost, so only the read/enforce side was missing — enforcement is now symmetric.
effect: 552 tests pass (3 new); clippy clean; zero new deps; behaviour-preserving for the buffered path (same logic, now shared); no change when budget/spike unset. IMP-14 difficulty-signal escalation remains buffered-only by design (quality-only, Local->Cloud, needs embeddings).
grounding: ADR-138; ADR-137 (same bug class); IMP-26 (ADR-129); FrugalGPT arXiv:2305.05176 cost control
risk: Low — closes a cost-control bypass; opt-in feature; over-budget streaming now behaves exactly like over-budget buffered (429 or local redirect)

title: OTel span on the streaming path (IMP-23 fix, ADR-139)
change: proxy.rs stream_chat_to_socket(): start a telemetry::Span before backend.stream_complete when otel_log is set (same gen_ai.system derivation as run_completion); on Ok completion fill response_model/input_tokens/output_tokens/route/finish_reason=stop, finish(), append_to(log_path). Mirrors the buffered emit at run_completion. proxy_tests.rs: 2 tests (streaming writes a valid gen_ai.chat span with pasture.route; control: no otel_log => disabled).
reason: Socratic review (third application of the ADR-138 checklist: which run_completion behaviours are missing from stream_chat_to_socket?). OTel span emission (IMP-23) was buffered-path only. PASTURE_OTEL_LOG silently dropped every stream:true request, so the trace log omitted the most common client mode (streaming). Observability that drops streaming is a defect for anyone relying on the trace log.
effect: 554 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps; off by default; errors emit no span (matches buffered path). Response caching on the streaming path left out of scope: serving a cached completion as a synthesized SSE stream is a semantics change (chunking/usage chunk/fingerprint) deserving its own design; it is a missed optimization, not a correctness/cost/observability defect.
grounding: ADR-139; ADR-138/ADR-137 (same bug class); IMP-23 (ADR-133); OTel GenAI SemConv 1.28+
risk: Low — additive observability; span emitted only on successful streamed completion; file I/O errors are non-fatal (logged to stderr)

title: Correct gen_ai.system in OTel spans (IMP-23 fix, ADR-140)
change: proxy.rs: added cloud_system: String field + with_cloud_system(&str) builder; added otel_system_for(route)->String (Cloud => cloud_system or 'cloud'; Local => local backend name() or 'local'). Both span emit sites (run_completion buffered, stream_chat_to_socket streaming) now set span.system = self.otel_system_for(route) after completion. Removed the creation-time system guess (Span::start("", model); system filled on completion). cli.rs run_serve: .with_cloud_system(&config.cloud_provider). proxy_tests.rs: 2 tests (cloud span reports provider 'anthropic'; local route not mislabeled 'cloud' nor cloud provider).
reason: Socratic review of what IMP-23 actually writes: gen_ai.system is an OTel GenAI attribute identifying the provider (openai/anthropic/ollama), but pasture emitted the placeholder 'cloud'/'local'. Worse, it was computed at span creation from whether a cloud backend was merely configured (Some(name)=="cloud"), so a request that actually routed local while a cloud backend existed was mislabeled gen_ai.system='cloud' — only pasture.route reflected the true route. Two defects: non-compliant value and decoupled from the actual route.
effect: 556 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. gen_ai.system now reflects the backend that served the request: cloud routes report the configured provider, local routes report the local backend name. A fallback-provider completion still reports the primary provider name (minor, documented).
grounding: ADR-140; ADR-139/138/137 (IMP-23 line); OTel GenAI SemConv gen_ai.system
risk: Low — observability-only attribute correction; value now matches the real route; no behaviour change to routing or responses

title: Daily token budget resets at UTC midnight (IMP-26 fix, ADR-141)
change: proxy.rs: added budget_day: AtomicU64 field (days since epoch the today_cloud_tokens counter belongs to); init in new() to unix_now()/86400; with_budget anchors it to the current day when seeding the counter. Added roll_budget_day_if_needed(): if the current UTC day != stored budget_day, compare_exchange the day and (winner only) reset today_cloud_tokens to 0. Called at the top of check_budget_and_spike and before the cloud token fetch_add in log_cost. proxy_tests.rs: 2 tests (over-budget counter anchored to a past day resets and the request reaches cloud; same-day over-budget still blocks with 429).
reason: Socratic review of the budget guard's time semantics: today_cloud_tokens was seeded from the cost log at startup and only ever incremented, never reset at UTC day rollover. For a long-running pasture serve process (the documented deployment) the daily budget silently became cumulative-since-startup after the first midnight — once exceeded, every request was capped to local (or 429'd) until restart. Day-1 looked correct only because the startup seed reads today's log. The comment even claimed 'cumulative cloud tokens since UTC midnight' but nothing enforced the reset.
effect: 558 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps; std-only lazy reset (no timer thread / no async); spike counters (all-time avg) intentionally unaffected. Multi-process deployments already keep per-process counters; reset-to-0 is consistent with that.
grounding: ADR-141; IMP-26 (ADR-129); ADR-138 (budget guard streaming parity)
risk: Low — corrects daily semantics; same-day enforcement unchanged (verified by control test); reset performed by exactly one thread via compare_exchange

title: Authenticate before rate-limiting (IMP-15 fix, ADR-142)
change: proxy.rs check_gate(): moved the auth_token check ahead of the rate_limiter check. /health still returns None (exempt from both) at the top. Now an unauthenticated request returns 401 without calling rl.allow(), so it consumes no token; only authenticated requests are metered. proxy_tests.rs: 1 test (5 anonymous requests are each 401 and do not drain a 1-token bucket; the authenticated client is then admitted, and its follow-up is 429).
reason: Socratic review of the exposed-deployment security surface: check_gate metered before authenticating. With both PASTURE_AUTH_TOKEN and PASTURE_RATE_LIMIT enabled, an unauthenticated request consumed a token from the single global bucket before receiving its 401. An attacker who does not know the token could flood the proxy, drain the bucket, and 429 the legitimate authenticated client — turning the rate limit (meant to protect the server) into a DoS lever for an anonymous party. Standard practice is authenticate-then-meter so the budget is spent only by legitimate traffic.
effect: 559 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Auth check is near-zero cost (existing constant-time compare over a short token), so checking it first does not create a new flood surface. The token bucket itself was already correct; only gate ordering changed. Existing tests exercised auth and rate-limit separately, so none regressed.
grounding: ADR-142; IMP-15; auth_ok/constant_time_eq (ADR pre-existing); OWASP authenticate-before-expensive-work
risk: Low — reorders two cheap checks; /health remains open; no behaviour change when only one of auth/rate-limit is configured

title: OTel spans emitted on backend failures (IMP-23 fix, ADR-143)
change: telemetry.rs: Span gains status: &'static str (default 'ok') and error_message: Option<String>; to_jsonl() emits self.status instead of the hardcoded 'ok' literal and conditionally appends a pasture.error attribute. proxy.rs buffered path: converted the three-way completion `?` into an explicit match so the Err arm sets span.status='error', span.error_message, span.route/system and appends the span before returning Err(e). proxy.rs streaming path: the Err(e) arm now fills and appends an error span before writing the SSE error frame. telemetry.rs: 2 tests (error span has status:error + pasture.error; ok span has neither). proxy_tests.rs: 2 tests (buffered and streaming backend failure each emit an error span).
reason: Socratic review of the PASTURE_OTEL_LOG observability story: 'what does an operator see in the trace log when a cloud call fails?' The answer was nothing — both paths only emitted a span on success (buffered propagated ProxyError via ?, streaming wrote an SSE error frame and skipped the span). A sustained backend outage left the trace log blank, which is the opposite of what tracing exists for: errors are exactly what an operator needs to see. to_jsonl() also hardcoded status:'ok', so even a manually-constructed error span would have been mislabeled.
effect: 563 tests pass (4 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Operators now see backend failures in the trace log with status:error and a pasture.error message (no PII — error strings are backend transport/protocol messages, not prompt content). Success spans are byte-identical to before (status defaults to 'ok', no pasture.error attribute).
grounding: ADR-143; IMP-23 (ADR-129/139/140); OTel span status semantic convention
risk: Low — observability-only addition; success path unchanged; error path still returns the same ProxyError / SSE frame, now additionally traced

title: OTel spans emitted for cache hits (IMP-23 fix, ADR-144)
change: proxy.rs: moved OTel span creation from after the completion call to immediately after classify_and_decide(), ahead of the exact-match and semantic cache lookups. Added emit_cache_hit_span(&mut Option<Span>, &resp, route_label) helper that sets system=route_label, response_model, input/output tokens, route, finish_reason='stop', finishes and appends. Both cache-hit early returns (exact 'cache', semantic 'semantic_cache') now call it before returning. Removed the now-duplicate span creation in the backend path. proxy_tests.rs: 1 test (a cached request emits a span with pasture.route='cache'; both miss and hit are traced; cache-hit span is valid JSON).
reason: Socratic review of the OTel trace schema vs. behaviour: telemetry.rs documents pasture.route values 'local','cloud','cache', but no code path ever emitted route='cache'. Cache hits return Ok((hit,'cache',None)) before the span was created (span was started after the cache checks), so an operator measuring cache hit-rate or latency through PASTURE_OTEL_LOG saw zero cache traffic — the documented route value was literally unreachable. The cache is the cheapest, highest-value path to observe, and it was the one invisible to tracing.
effect: 564 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Cache hits (exact and semantic) now appear in the trace log with pasture.route='cache'/'semantic_cache' and gen_ai.system set to the route label (no upstream provider exists for a cache hit). No PII: cached responses carry only token counts and model name into the span, never content. Backend completion spans are unchanged (same fields, created at the same effective point relative to the call).
grounding: ADR-144; ADR-143/140/139 (IMP-23 line); telemetry.rs pasture.route schema; OTel GenAI SemConv
risk: Low — observability-only addition; cache lookup/return semantics unchanged; success and error backend spans unaffected

title: Accept array-form message content (OpenAI multimodal shape, ADR-145)
change: proxy.rs: added extract_message_content(&JsonValue)->Result<String,ProxyError> that accepts content as a JSON string (unchanged) or as an OpenAI array-of-parts ([{type:text,text:...}, ...]). Text parts (type=='text', or a bare {text:...} with no explicit type) are concatenated newline-joined; any non-text part (image_url/input_audio/file/etc.) returns 400 'unsupported content part'. parse_request now calls it instead of the inline .as_str().ok_or(...). SPEC.md §3.1 updated to document string-or-text-array. proxy_tests.rs: 4 tests (array text accepted and flattened to 'hello\nworld'; email inside an array part still classified as PII; image_url part rejected; truly-missing content still 400).
reason: Socratic review of the OpenAI-compatibility claim: real OpenAI accepts content as an array of parts, and the official SDK's vision helper plus LangChain et al. emit array-of-parts content even for plain text. parse_request read content with .as_str(), which only matches JsonValue::Str, so every array-form request was rejected with 400 'message missing content'. The proxy advertised OpenAI compatibility but rejected a standard, widely-emitted request shape. (Not a privacy leak — array content was fail-closed/rejected — but a genuine compatibility defect.)
effect: 568 tests pass (4 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Array text content is now flattened and routed; the flattened text flows through routing_text()->privacy classify(), so the PII guard is unchanged (proven by a test that an email in an array part is still detected and kept local). Genuine multimodal parts are rejected with a clear 400 rather than silently dropped, keeping the text router honest (it never answers a vision request as if the image were absent).
grounding: ADR-145; SPEC §3.1; OpenAI chat-completions content-parts schema; IMP-3 privacy guard parity
risk: Low — widens an input shape that was previously a hard 400; string content path byte-identical; non-text parts still rejected; no behaviour change to routing, caching, or backends beyond receiving flattened text

title: Empty local answer always escalates in cascade (IMP-1 fix, ADR-146)
change: cascade.rs should_escalate(): added an early `if answer.trim().chars().count() < 2 { return true }` guard before the mean_logprob match, so an empty/near-empty local answer escalates regardless of the logprob. The logprob (Some(lp) => lp < threshold) and text-heuristic (None => is_low_confidence) branches now govern only the non-empty case. cascade.rs tests: 1 test (empty/whitespace/1-char answers escalate even with a confident logprob like 0.0; a confident non-empty answer 'Paris.' with lp -0.1 still stays local).
reason: Socratic review of the cascade confidence logic: should_escalate treated mean_logprob as a complete replacement for the text heuristic (match mean_logprob { Some(lp) => lp < threshold, None => is_low_confidence }). But token-logprob (answer-quality uncertainty) and 'the model emitted nothing' are orthogonal: a local model can return an empty string or a lone EOS token while reporting a high mean logprob (e.g. 0.0). With a -1.0 threshold, 0.0 < -1.0 is false, so the request stayed local and the user got a blank answer when the cloud could have answered. The is_low_confidence heuristic already escalates empty answers, but the logprob branch bypassed it.
effect: 569 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Empty/near-empty local answers now always escalate to cloud (when cascade is enabled and a cloud backend exists). Zero false-positive cost — an empty answer is never a useful local result. Non-empty behaviour is unchanged: logprob still governs subtle uncertainty, text heuristic still used when no logprob is available.
grounding: ADR-146; IMP-1 (FrugalGPT arXiv:2305.05176); arXiv:2605.02241 mean-logprob routing; is_low_confidence empty-answer rule
risk: Low — adds escalation only for the empty-answer case, which was previously a silent blank-response bug; falls back to local if the cloud call then fails (existing complete_cascade behaviour)

title: Streaming exact-match cache parity (ADR-147)
change: proxy.rs stream_chat_to_socket(): capture sensitive from classify_and_decide (was discarded). Added an exact-match cache READ right after classify_and_decide and BEFORE apply_budget_guard (matching the buffered ordering so a hit is served even when over budget): on hit, write SSE headers and replay hit.content as one chunk with route 'cache', emit an ADR-144 cache-hit OTel span, log_cost('cache', ...) (free), then stop chunk + optional usage chunk + [DONE], and return — no backend call. Added a cache WRITE at the end of the Ok(r) arm: store the completed response, restoring PII via a cloned pseudonymize mapping (cache_mapping) before put() so the cache never holds <EMAIL_n> tokens (defensive parity — pseudonymized requests are sensitive and thus uncached anyway). cache_key = (!sensitive).then(request_key(req)); None when sensitive (I2). Semantic cache intentionally left buffered-only (stream path computes no query embedding). proxy_tests.rs: added roundtrip_ref(&Proxy,...) borrowing helper + 4 tests (buffered-warm then streamed hit serves 'cache'; streamed miss then buffered hit; sensitive stream neither reads nor writes cache; no-cache control never hits). SPEC.md §6 cache bullet updated.
reason: Socratic review of the session's dominant bug class (buffered-only features missing on the streaming path): the exact-match cache served buffered requests but stream_chat_to_socket never consulted or populated it. Identical streaming prompts paid full backend cost every time, and a streamed answer never warmed the cache for later buffered hits. The streaming path also discarded the sensitivity flag from classify_and_decide, so the cache gate had to be re-derived.
effect: 573 tests pass (4 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. stream:true requests now serve from and populate the exact-match cache with the same sensitivity gating (I2) and free-cost/route='cache' semantics as buffered, including an ADR-144 cache-hit OTel span. Over-budget cached prompts are still served (cache checked before the budget guard, matching buffered). No behaviour change when PASTURE_CACHE is unset (control test).
grounding: ADR-147; ADR-144 (cache-hit spans); IMP-31 (parse parity); buffered cache ordering in run_completion; I2 sensitive-never-cached
risk: Medium-low — touches the delicate streaming path, but the cache gate mirrors the audited buffered path exactly, sensitive content is excluded (tested), pseudonymized content is restored before caching (tested gate: sensitive→uncached), and a no-cache control test confirms no behaviour change when the cache is off

title: Detect IPv6 addresses as sensitive (IMP-3 fix, ADR-148)
change: privacy.rs: added looks_like_ipv6(token) — trims wrapping non-(hexdigit|colon) punctuation, requires >= 2 colons, then parses with std::net::Ipv6Addr::from_str. classify()'s ip check changed from `any(looks_like_ipv4)` to `any(|t| looks_like_ipv4(t) || looks_like_ipv6(t))`, keeping the single shared 'ip' category (no double-push). privacy.rs tests: 2 tests (positives: 2001:db8::1, fe80::1, ::1, full 8-group, bracketed [..], trailing comma, classify surfaces 'ip'; negatives: 10:30, 10:30:45, a:b, std::vector, https://example.com, plain sentence stays non-sensitive).
reason: Socratic review of privacy-detector coverage: classify flagged IPv4 (four dot-separated octets) as sensitive and forced it local, but had no IPv6 detection at all, so a prompt containing 2001:db8::1 was classified non-sensitive and could leak to the cloud. SPEC's explicit bias is that a false negative (data leak) is unacceptable while a false positive (stays local) is cheap — the gap sat on the unacceptable side, and IPv6 identifies a host exactly as IPv4 does.
effect: 575 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps (std Ipv6Addr parser). IPv6 addresses now force local routing under the shared 'ip' category. Near-zero false positives: the >=2-colon pre-check plus std parser reject clock times (10:30:45), ranges (a:b), C++ scope tokens (std::vector), and URLs.
grounding: ADR-148; IMP-3 (PRISM arXiv:2511.22788); SPEC §5 over-classify bias; existing looks_like_ipv4 parity
risk: Low — adds detection (more force-local), the safe direction per SPEC; std parser is authoritative for IPv6 validity; negative tests guard the common false-positive shapes

title: Prompt framing parity for streaming: system prompt + context (ADR-149)
change: proxy.rs: extracted frame_request(&self, req)->Option<CompletionRequest> that applies the user system prompt (prepend_system_prompt) then the date/OS context (inject_context_into), returning None when neither is configured (caller keeps the borrow, no clone). run_completion now calls it (replacing its two inline with_sys/injected blocks). stream_chat_to_socket now calls it after the injection guard and before classify_and_decide, rebinding req. proxy_tests.rs: 2 tests using RecordingEchoBackend as the local backend (streaming request's recorded routing_text contains the configured system prompt; control with no system prompt sees only the user text).
reason: Socratic review for remaining buffered/streaming asymmetries (the session's dominant bug class): run_completion applied PASTURE_SYSTEM_PROMPT and inject_context (date/OS) before routing, but stream_chat_to_socket applied neither. A stream:true request therefore silently lost the user's configured system prompt and grounding context, and because framing is part of routing_text it could even be classified/routed differently than the same request sent buffered.
effect: 577 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Streaming requests now receive identical framing to buffered ones, applied after the injection guard (which still scans the original request, matching buffered order) and before classify_and_decide so framing feeds routing. The shared frame_request() helper means the two paths can no longer drift. No clone when neither feature is configured.
grounding: ADR-149; ADR-137/138/139/143/147 (buffered/streaming parity line); prepend_system_prompt + inject_context_into (IMP-context)
risk: Low — buffered behaviour is byte-identical (same two steps, same order, now via a helper); streaming gains the missing framing; control test confirms no framing when unconfigured

title: Streaming embedding parity: semantic cache + difficulty signal (ADR-150)
change: proxy.rs: added enum EmbeddingStep{SemanticHit(CompletionResponse), Proceed{route,embedding}} and method embedding_step(req,route,sensitive,&mut otel_span) that computes the query embedding once (local /embeddings, skipped when sensitive), checks the semantic cache (emitting a cache-hit span on hit), and applies the IMP-14 difficulty escalation; returns SemanticHit or Proceed{(maybe escalated) route, embedding}. Extracted write_cached_stream(sock,cors,&hit,route_label,include_usage) for SSE replay (headers, content chunk, free log_cost, stop, optional usage, [DONE]), now used by both the exact-match ('cache') and semantic ('semantic_cache') streaming hit paths. Refactored run_completion (buffered) onto embedding_step — byte-identical behaviour. stream_chat_to_socket now: starts the OTel span before the cache checks, serves exact then semantic hits via write_cached_stream, runs embedding_step to (a) serve semantic hits and (b) escalate the route before apply_budget_guard, and on a successful miss stores the restored content into BOTH the exact and semantic caches (restored once, reused). proxy_tests.rs: 4 tests (streaming difficulty escalation to cloud; streamed semantic hit after a buffered warm; streamed miss populates the semantic cache for a later buffered hit; sensitive stream skips the semantic cache).
reason: Final sweep for the session's dominant buffered/streaming asymmetry: run_completion computed a query embedding once and used it for the semantic cache (IMP-12) and the difficulty signal (IMP-14), but stream_chat_to_socket computed no embedding at all. A stream:true request therefore re-ran the backend on a semantic match and was never pre-escalated near a known-hard centroid — silently degraded vs the same request buffered. Two opt-in features were missing on one path.
effect: 581 tests pass (4 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Streaming now has full parity with buffered for the semantic cache and difficulty signal, sharing embedding_step() and write_cached_stream() so the paths cannot drift. All embedding features remain opt-in (default build unaffected) and sensitive content never triggers an embedding (I5). Buffered behaviour is byte-identical after the refactor (existing 577 tests unchanged).
grounding: ADR-150; ADR-147 (exact-cache streaming); IMP-12 (semantic cache, GPTCache/arXiv:2603.03301); IMP-14 (difficulty, routing survey arXiv:2506.06579); buffered run_completion as the reference
risk: Medium-low — touches the delicate streaming path, but the logic is the shared helper extracted from the audited buffered path; embedding features are opt-in; sensitive content is excluded (tested); a no-embedding default path is unchanged

title: Incremental cost summary for /metrics and /v1/stats (ADR-151)
change: cost.rs: extracted fold_record(&mut CostSummary, &LoggedRecord) from summarize (summarize now folds via it; total starts at 0 and increments per record). proxy.rs: added field metrics_cache: Mutex<(u64 bytes_consumed, CostSummary)> (init (0, summarize(&[]))); added live_cost_summary() that stats the cost-log length, resets the cache if the file shrank (rotation/truncation), else seeks to bytes_consumed, reads new bytes, folds only complete \n-terminated lines (partial trailing line left for next call), advances bytes_consumed, and returns the cached summary clone. handle_stats and handle_metrics now call live_cost_summary() instead of read_log()+summarize(). proxy_tests.rs: 2 tests (incremental summary equals a fresh full read_log+summarize across appends, every field; truncating the log resets the cache to reflect only new content).
reason: Socratic review of the observability endpoints' cost: /metrics exists for Prometheus to scrape every few seconds, but each call to /metrics and /v1/stats re-read and re-parsed the ENTIRE cost log via read_log()+summarize(). The cost log grows by one line per request and is never rotated, so on a long-running server each scrape became an O(log-size) operation growing without bound — the exact workload Prometheus stresses. The aggregate (route counts/tokens/spend) is foldable, so it can be maintained incrementally.
effect: 583 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. /metrics and /v1/stats now fold only newly-appended lines per call (O(new bytes) instead of O(whole log)). Output is byte-identical to the full re-read (test compares every field). Truncation/rotation is detected via file-length shrink and resets the cache. The pasture stats CLI (one-shot) still reads the whole log. Single complete-line consumption avoids miscounting a half-written record during a racing scrape.
grounding: ADR-151; IMP-metrics (/v1/stats), IMP-metrics-prom (/metrics); cost::summarize/fold_record; Prometheus scrape model
risk: Low — output is byte-identical to the previous full re-read (proven by test); cache is per-process behind a Mutex; truncation handled; worst case on a poisoned lock returns an error like the previous read error path

title: Authoritative loopback detection for the exposed-without-auth warning (ADR-152)
change: cli.rs: added listen_addr_is_loopback(addr)->bool that parses the listen address with std::net (SocketAddr then IpAddr) and returns ip().is_loopback(); a non-numeric host is loopback only when literally 'localhost'. run_serve's security nudge now uses it instead of the inline string-prefix heuristic (addr.starts_with("127.")||"localhost"||"[::1]"||"::1"). cli.rs tests: 1 test asserting loopback forms (127/8, [::1]:port, ::1, localhost[:port], expanded [0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]) are local and exposed forms (0.0.0.0, [::], LAN IP, non-localhost hostname, and the global ::1:2:3:4) are not.
reason: New Socratic angle requested by the user (string heuristic vs authoritative parsing): the exposed-without-auth security warning gated on a string-prefix loopback check. Verified against the old logic, it had two defects — it false-warned on a real loopback bind in expanded IPv6 form ([0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:8080 matched no prefix → 'exposed'), and, security-relevant, it suppressed the warning for a GLOBAL address that merely starts with '::1' (bare ::1:2:3:4 = 0:0:0:0:1:2:3:4, yet starts_with("::1") is true → treated as localhost → no warning). A security gate must not guess exposure from string prefixes.
effect: 584 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. title: Don't hold the centroid lock across I/O or the per-request cosine (IMP-14 concurrency, ADR-154)

title: Semantic cache keyed by requested model (ADR-158)
change: cache.rs SemanticCache: entries changed from VecDeque<(Vec<f64>, CompletionResponse)> to VecDeque<(Vec<f64>, String, CompletionResponse)>; find_similar(query, model) skips entries whose stored model != the requested model; put(embedding, model, resp) stores the model. proxy.rs embedding_step: find_similar now passes &req.model; run_completion semantic-cache put passes req.model.clone(); finalize_streamed gains a req_model:&str parameter (passed as &req.model at both the streaming call site and the two tests in proxy_tests.rs); the put inside finalize_streamed passes req_model.to_string(). cache.rs tests: 1 new test (test_semantic_cache_different_model_is_miss: same embedding stored for 'llama3', queried for 'gpt-4o' → miss; queried for 'llama3' → hit). Two requests for the same prompt content but different model names produce the same embedding (same local embeddings backend), so the second request got a cache hit serving the first model's response — wrong model, wrong output. A 'gpt-4o' request could silently receive a cached 'llama3' answer and vice versa.
effect: 590 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Same-model semantic hits work as before; cross-model false hits are now impossible. The SemanticCache API change is confined to cache.rs + the three proxy.rs call sites + the two direct tests.
grounding: ADR-158; cache.rs request_key (exact-match cache model key as reference); IMP-12 (semantic cache)

title: Semantic cache keyed by sampling parameters too (extends ADR-158, ADR-159)

grounding: ADR-159; ADR-158 (model key); cache.rs request_key sampling-key invariant; IMP-sampling (sampling passthrough); IMP-12 (semantic cache)

title: PASTURE_CACHE_TTL bounds the semantic cache too (extends ADR-158/159, ADR-160)
change: cache.rs: SemanticCache gained max_age:Option<Duration> and a per-entry Instant; the entry tuple was refactored to a named SemanticEntry{embedding,model,sampling,inserted,resp} struct. Added set_max_age(secs) and max_age_secs() mirroring ResponseCache. find_similar now self.entries.retain(|e| e.inserted.elapsed()<=max_age) before scoring, so an expired entry is a miss and frees its slot. proxy.rs with_cache_ttl(): now also applies set_max_age to self.semantic_cache. cli.rs: reordered .with_semantic_cache before .with_cache_ttl so the semantic cache exists when the TTL is applied. cache.rs tests: 2 new (expired semantic entry is a miss and removed; no-TTL entry survives).

title: Cascade escalations respect the daily budget / spike guard (IMP-26 enforcement hole, ADR-161)

Same evasion class as ADR-155 (under-enforcing a budget control is the unsafe direction).

Cascade cloud escalations now pass the same budget/spike guard as the direct cloud path; over-budget escalations degrade gracefully to the local answer (cascade always has one), so a budget cap never turns a cascade into a 429. title: Atomic JSONL appends to the cost and trace logs (concurrency, ADR-162)
change: cost.rs CostRecord::append_to and telemetry.rs Span::append_to: replaced writeln!(f, "{}", self.to_jsonl()) with f.write_all(format!("{}\n", self.to_jsonl()).as_bytes()) — building the line plus newline once and writing it in a single write_all. cost.rs tests: 1 new (8 threads x 64 concurrent appends; asserts every physical line parses via parse_log_line and read_log returns all 512 records, i.e. none lost to interleaving). Verified the test fails 5/5 against the old writeln! and passes with the fix.

New Socratic angle — concurrency on the append-only logs: the thread-per-connection server calls log_cost (and OTel span append) from many threads at once. writeln! issues two syscalls (content, then 
); O_APPEND makes each individual write atomic but not a pair, so two threads can interleave as content_A, content_B, 
,
