No corruption or record loss under concurrent appends. Output format is byte-identical to before (still one JSONL line per record).
grounding: ADR-162; append_access_log (existing single-write_all pattern); POSIX O_APPEND per-write atomicity; thread-per-connection server
risk: Low — same bytes written, only the syscall boundary changes (two writes -> one); matches the already-correct access-log path; regression test proven to catch the old behaviour

title: Budget daily-cap TOCTOU: atomic pre-reservation in check_budget_and_spike (ADR-163)
change: proxy.rs check_budget_and_spike: replaced load(Relaxed)+compare with fetch_add(estimated_tokens)+compare-prev+fetch_sub-on-fail (atomic pre-reservation). apply_budget_guard return type changed from Result<Route,ProxyError> to Result<(Route,u64),ProxyError> — u64 is the reserved token count (0 for non-cloud or warn/local-only paths). complete_cascade/complete_cloud_with_fallback/complete_direct return types gain a u64 element (cascade's inner reservation; 0 for the others). run_completion return type gains u64 (effective_reserved = cascade_reserved + budget_reserved_outer; exactly one is non-zero). complete_cascade rolls back the cascade reservation on cloud failure. log_cost gains reserved_tokens:u64 — reconciles (add/sub the actual-estimated difference) when reserved>0; adds actual post-hoc when reserved==0 (warn-action path). When route_label=local but reserved>0 (fallback case) log_cost fetches_sub the reservation. finalize_streamed gains reserved_tokens:u64 passed to log_cost. stream_chat_to_socket: unpacks (route,budget_reserved) from apply_budget_guard; passes budget_reserved to finalize_streamed; rolls back budget_reserved in the Err(e) arm. proxy_tests.rs: finalize_streamed calls gain trailing 0; 1 new test (test_budget_pre_reservation_blocks_at_ceiling).
reason: Socratic angle — TOCTOU in the daily budget check: check_budget_and_spike read today_cloud_tokens with load(Relaxed), compared against the daily budget, then returned. log_cost performed the actual fetch_add only after the cloud response arrived — an entire RTT later. Two concurrent cloud requests could both read 'under budget' and both proceed, overshooting the cap by up to one request's worth of tokens. The race window is enormous (seconds to minutes for cloud LLM calls). The 'block' action was supposed to be a hard cap, but two simultaneous requests near the limit could both pass it.
effect: 598 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Budget pre-reservation is now atomic: at most one concurrent request can win the reservation when the counter is near the ceiling; the loser's reservation is rolled back immediately. Existing cascade-budget tests (ADR-161) pass unchanged. The warn-action path is unaffected (proceeds without pre-reservation, adds actual post-hoc). The budget counter now tracks estimated-then-reconciled tokens rather than post-hoc actuals — accuracy is unchanged in practice (MockBackend returns 0 tokens; real backends typically return counts close to estimates).
grounding: ADR-163; IMP-26 (budget guard); ADR-161 (cascade budget guard); TOCTOU race pattern
risk: Medium — touches the core budget accounting path; compensated by: (a) existing cascade/budget tests still pass; (b) new ceiling test covers the rollback; (c) the warn-action path (reserved=0, add-actual) is identical to the old code; (d) local routes are completely unaffected (early-return fast path unchanged)

title: Budget token release saturates at 0 across a UTC day rollover (ADR-164)
change: proxy.rs: added release_cloud_tokens(n:u64) — a fetch_update CAS loop applying saturating_sub to today_cloud_tokens — and replaced all five ADR-163 fetch_sub sites with it (check_budget_and_spike reservation rollback; log_cost reconcile-down; log_cost local-fallback release; complete_cascade cloud-failure rollback; stream_chat_to_socket error rollback). The log_cost reconciliation if/else-if was rewritten as match tokens.cmp(&reserved_tokens) {Greater=>fetch_add, Less=>release_cloud_tokens, Equal=>noop} (also clears the clippy comparison_chain lint). proxy_tests.rs: 2 new tests (test_budget_reconcile_does_not_underflow_across_day_rollover; test_budget_local_fallback_release_does_not_underflow) — both drive log_cost with today_cloud_tokens=0 and reserved>actual (the post-rollover state) and assert the counter clamps at 0; both fail against wrapping_sub.
reason: Socratic angle turned on ADR-163 itself: ADR-163 introduced subtraction on today_cloud_tokens, but that counter is reset to 0 by roll_budget_day_if_needed at UTC midnight. A request reserving estimated tokens near 23:59:59 spends the cloud RTT (seconds) crossing midnight; log_cost then rolls the day (counter->0) and reconciles fetch_sub(reserved-actual), underflowing 0 to ~u64::MAX. The bare rollback paths underflow too via a concurrent day roll. The wrapped counter (~1.8e19) dwarfs any budget, so for the rest of the new day every cloud request is blocked/redirected to local — a single midnight-straddling request silently disables the cloud route until the next midnight. Same control-enforcement failure class as ADR-155/161, in the release direction.
effect: 600 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. All budget releases now clamp at 0 instead of wrapping. No behaviour change away from the day boundary (saturating_sub == plain sub when counter>=n). The reconcile match is equivalent to the prior if-chain plus the saturating release.
grounding: ADR-164; ADR-163 (pre-reservation that introduced the fetch_subs); ADR-155 (budget day-roll safe direction); IMP-26 (budget guard); u64 underflow / saturating arithmetic
risk: Low — purely defensive: replaces plain subtraction with saturating subtraction at five sites, identical when the counter is >= the amount; the only changed behaviour is clamping the wrap that previously bricked the cloud route for a day; covered by two regression tests proven to catch wrapping_sub

title: Daily token budget is observable on /metrics and /v1/stats (ADR-165)
change: proxy.rs: added Proxy::budget_snapshot()->(u64,u64) returning (today_cloud_tokens, budget_daily_tokens) after calling roll_budget_day_if_needed (so a new-day scrape reads 0). build_metrics_response and build_stats_response gain budget_used:u64 and budget_limit:u64 parameters (both annotated #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]). build_metrics_response emits two new Prometheus gauges (pasture_budget_daily_tokens_used, pasture_budget_daily_tokens_limit). build_stats_response emits budget_daily_tokens_used and budget_daily_tokens_limit JSON fields. handle_metrics and handle_stats call budget_snapshot and pass the pair through. proxy_tests.rs: updated the 2 builder unit tests to pass+assert the new args; 2 new end-to-end tests (test_stats_exposes_live_daily_budget pre-seeds the counter and checks handle_stats surfaces used+limit; test_budget_gauge_reads_zero_on_new_day anchors the counter to yesterday and asserts the gauge reads 0).

An operator setting PASTURE_BUDGET_DAILY_TOKENS had no way to see how close they were to the cap — the metrics endpoints exposed only all-time cost-log totals (route counts, tokens, spend), never today_cloud_tokens or the limit. The first sign of an exhausted budget was requests silently routing local (or 429ing in block mode), with no gauge to anticipate it or capacity-plan. A control you cannot observe is a control you cannot trust.
effect: 602 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. /metrics and /v1/stats now expose used-vs-limit for the daily budget. The snapshot rolls the UTC day first so a new-day scrape reads 0 (not a stale total) and reflects the same enforcement counter — including in-flight ADR-163 reservations — that gates the next request. Token counts only (no PII, I3); both endpoints remain behind the existing auth gate (IMP-15).
grounding: ADR-165; IMP-26 (daily budget enforcement); IMP-metrics / IMP-metrics-prom (/v1/stats + Prometheus /metrics); ADR-163 (reservation counter the gauge reflects); ADR-155 (day-roll semantics); observability principle (a control you can't observe you can't trust)
risk: Low — additive read-only gauges over an existing in-memory counter; no enforcement behaviour changes; budget_snapshot's only side effect (rolling the day on read) is the same reset the next request would perform and is the correct value to report; new-day test pins the behaviour

title: Optional cloud pricing makes cloud_cost_usd a real number (ADR-166)
change: proxy.rs: new field cloud_price_per_1m:(f64,f64) (default (0.0,0.0)); builder with_cloud_price(input,output) clamping negative/non-finite to 0; helper cloud_cost_usd(prompt,completion) = prompt/1e6*in + completion/1e6*out; log_cost now computes cost for route_label=="cloud" (local/cache stay 0.0) and passes it to CostRecord::new instead of the hardcoded 0.0. config.rs: new field cloud_price_per_1m:(f64,f64); parse_price_pair("<in>,<out>") helper (rejects missing field/non-numeric/negative/non-finite); env var PASTURE_CLOUD_PRICE_PER_1M and config-file key cloud_price_per_1m. cli.rs: .with_cloud_price(...) in the serve builder chain; serve banner prints the configured price. Cloud-only (local/cache free). Bad prices clamp to 0 so a misconfiguration cannot yield a negative or NaN spend total. Token counts only, no PII (I3).
grounding: ADR-166; ADR-165 (budget observability, sibling metric); IMP-metrics / IMP-metrics-prom (the spend gauges this populates); cost.rs CostRecord/cost_usd; BYOK / no-stale-hardcoded-pricing philosophy
risk: Low — additive and opt-in: default (0,0) preserves the prior always-0 behaviour exactly; pricing only multiplies token counts the proxy already records; inputs validated and clamped at both parse (parse_price_pair) and apply (with_cloud_price) so no negative/NaN can reach the spend total

title: Monitoring endpoints exempt from rate limiter (ADR-167)
change: proxy.rs check_gate(): inserted a path-exempt check after auth but before the token-bucket consumption — requests to /metrics and /v1/stats return None (allowed) without decrementing the bucket. The exemption comment explains the Prometheus-scraper conflict and the /v1/* scope mismatch. proxy_tests.rs: 2 new tests (test_monitoring_endpoints_exempt_from_rate_limit: exhausts the bucket with /v1/models, then confirms /metrics and /v1/stats both pass; test_monitoring_endpoints_auth_still_enforced: with PASTURE_AUTH_TOKEN set both endpoints still return 401 without a token, and are admitted with the correct token).
reason: Socratic probe of check_gate: 'The rate limiter doc says it caps /v1/* requests. /metrics is not under /v1/ at all. Does it consume tokens?' Yes — check_gate had a single early-exit for /health, so every non-health path (including /metrics and the read-only /v1/stats) consumed the same fixed-capacity bucket as /v1/chat/completions. A standard Prometheus scraper at 15-second intervals (4 req/min) silently consumed 40% of a PASTURE_RATE_LIMIT=10 inference budget for zero inference work. With a tight limit this can prevent inference requests from being admitted at all during a scrape burst. The root defect: the exemption logic expressed 'exempt /health' when it should express 'exempt zero-cost read-only monitoring endpoints'.
effect: 611 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. /metrics and /v1/stats no longer consume rate-limit tokens. Auth is unchanged — PASTURE_AUTH_TOKEN still gates both endpoints. /v1/models remains rate-limited (within /v1/* scope). Behaviour unchanged when PASTURE_RATE_LIMIT is not set (rate_limiter=None; the new path check is evaluated but the early return is free and the None branch is unchanged).

title: StreamRestorer buffer is bounded — unterminated '<' can't stall the stream (ADR-168)
change: pseudonymize.rs: StreamRestorer gained a max_token_len:usize field computed in new() as max(token.len()) over the mapping (0 when empty). push() now, when the last '<' has no closing '>', flushes the entire pending buffer (split = pending.len()) once pending.len()-i >= max_token_len, instead of always holding from the dangling '<'. Below that length it still holds at i (the original split-token behaviour). 3 new tests (10_000-byte unterminated-'<' tail flushes with bounded held-back buffer; split token <EMA|IL_1> still restores after the bound; empty mapping never buffers and is pure pass-through).
reason: Socratic probe of the streaming PII-restore path (IMP-19): push() held back everything from the last unterminated '<' until finish(), to reassemble tokens (<EMAIL_1>) split across SSE deltas. The split-token case it was built for is correct, but a dangling '<' followed by a long run with no '>' — 'a < b' in code, or an adversarial/verbose cloud response emitting '<' then megabytes with no '>' — makes pending grow without bound: nothing is emitted until the stream ends, freezing SSE incremental delivery and amplifying memory. A real restore token is always short, so the hold-back never needs to exceed the longest mapping token.
effect: 614 tests pass (3 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. The held-back buffer is now bounded by the longest token (a token closes its '>' within max_token_len bytes, so past that the fragment provably cannot be a token — flushing it is correctness-preserving). The empty-mapping restorer never buffers (pure pass-through, consistent with restore being a no-op). The legitimate split-token case is unchanged (an in-progress token is shorter than max_token_len at each step, still held and restored). No PII ever flushed un-restored (proven by the existing per-delta-leak test plus the new split-after-bound test).
grounding: ADR-168; IMP-19 (reversible pseudonymization + streaming restore); ADR-156 (pseudonymizer token format <CATEGORY_N>); unbounded-buffer / streaming-stall failure class
risk: Low — the only changed behaviour is flushing (rather than indefinitely holding) a dangling-'<' fragment once it exceeds the longest mapping token, which provably cannot be a token; the held-token path for fragments shorter than max_token_len is unchanged; covered by a split-token regression test that exercises the boundary and the existing per-delta no-leak test

title: Spike-only guard (budget off) reports reserved=0 — no phantom-reservation reconcile (ADR-169)
change: proxy.rs apply_budget_guard: the success path (no spike, no budget-reject) now returns reserved = if budget_daily_tokens > 0 { estimated } else { 0 } instead of unconditionally returning estimated. The fetch_add pre-reservation in check_budget_and_spike is guarded by budget_daily_tokens > 0, so with spike detection alone no reservation exists and reserved must be 0 so log_cost takes the post-hoc fetch_add(actual) path rather than the reconciliation branch. proxy_tests.rs: 1 new test (test_spike_only_budget_off_gauge_tracks_actual_not_phantom_reservation) — budget off (0) + spike on (50), forces a cloud request via model:"cloud", asserts today_cloud_tokens equals the actual prompt+completion tokens (estimate_tokens("hi")+estimate_tokens("cloud-reply")); verified to FAIL against the pre-fix code (gauge clamped near 0) and pass after.
reason: Socratic probe of the budget/spike accounting after ADR-163 threaded pre-reservation through the call chain: apply_budget_guard's success path returned Ok((route, estimated)) unconditionally, but check_budget_and_spike only performs the fetch_add reservation inside `if budget_daily_tokens > 0`. So when spike detection is enabled but the daily budget is OFF, estimated (computed for the spike check) was returned as `reserved` though nothing was reserved. log_cost then took the reserved_tokens>0 reconciliation branch and adjusted today_cloud_tokens by tokens-reserved (or released reserved-tokens) as if estimated had been added — corrupting the gauge surfaced on /metrics and /v1/stats (ADR-165). Because the estimate leans high (routing over-predicts output for budget safety), the release dominated and the gauge clamped toward 0, under-reporting real cloud usage for any operator using spike detection without a daily cap.
effect: 615 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. With spike-on/budget-off, today_cloud_tokens now tracks actual cloud usage (post-hoc add) instead of a phantom-reservation delta, so the /metrics + /v1/stats usage gauge is correct. No behaviour change when the daily budget is active (reserved==estimated as before, a real reservation), when both guards are off (early return reserved=0), or on the spike/warn/local-only/block branches (already reserved=0 or Err). The `reserved` value now means strictly 'tokens reserved in today_cloud_tokens'.
grounding: ADR-169; ADR-163 (pre-reservation that introduced reserved_tokens threading); ADR-165 (the today_cloud_tokens gauge this corrupted); IMP-26 (budget/spike guard); control-accuracy failure class (ADR-163/164) in the observability direction
risk: Low — one-line semantics fix narrowing reserved to the case where a reservation truly happened; the budget-active path is unchanged; the only changed behaviour (budget-off/spike-on) routes log_cost to the already-tested post-hoc add path; covered by a regression test proven to catch the pre-fix gauge corruption

title: Streaming chunks share a single created timestamp (ADR-170)
change: proxy.rs: build_openai_chunk and build_openai_usage_chunk gained a created:u64 parameter (replacing the internal unix_now() call so the caller controls the timestamp). stream_chat_to_socket now captures let created = unix_now() once alongside id, model, and fp and passes it to all four chunk-builder call sites (delta callback, tail flush, stop chunk, usage chunk). write_cached_stream likewise captures created once and passes it to all three builder calls. proxy_tests.rs: all existing call sites updated with the new created argument (passing 0 for determinism); new regression test test_stream_chunks_share_created constructs three chunks (delta, stop, usage) with a fixed timestamp and asserts every chunk's created field matches.
reason: Socratic probe of the SSE streaming path: build_openai_chunk and build_openai_usage_chunk each called unix_now() internally, so every chunk in the same stream received a different created timestamp depending on when it was formatted. The OpenAI streaming API contract requires id, model, system_fingerprint, AND created to be identical across all chunks belonging to one completion — client SDKs and stream parsers use these fields to correlate chunks and assemble completions. A created clock that advances per-chunk breaks that correlation contract, can cause SDK chunk-rejection, and produces non-deterministic output that is impossible to test. The root defect: the function that formats a single chunk should not decide when 'now' is for a whole stream.
effect: 616 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. All chunks in a single stream now carry the same id, model, fingerprint, and created, satisfying the OpenAI streaming contract. Test call sites pass 0 (deterministic). No behaviour change at rest (build_openai_response was already correct — single unix_now() per buffered response). No impact on routing, caching, budgeting, or privacy paths.
grounding: ADR-170; OpenAI streaming API contract (id/model/fingerprint/created consistency across chunks); IMP-stream-chunks-share-model (preceding id/model/fp consistency fix this completes)
risk: Low — purely a parameter threading change; the only observable difference is the created field is now identical across chunks instead of incrementing per-chunk; covered by a regression test; write_cached_stream and stream_chat_to_socket are the only two call sites of the builders in production paths

title: GET /v1/models entries include required created field (ADR-171)
change: proxy.rs: build_models_response now calls unix_now() once per request and injects created:{now} into every model entry. build_model_response injects created:{unix_now()} into the single-model response. Both doc-comments updated to explain the OpenAI Model schema requirement and the request-time convention. proxy_tests.rs: 1 new test (test_models_response_includes_created_field) checks that both list entries and single-model entries carry a created:Number field using JsonValue::Number pattern match.
reason: Socratic probe of the /v1/models endpoint (IMP-8): build_models_response emitted {id, object, owned_by} — omitting the created (integer) field required by the OpenAI Model schema. The OpenAI Python SDK constructs a Model object with a non-optional created field; omitting it raises a ValidationError that prevents the client from listing or selecting models. Cursor uses the same schema. Other fields (id, object, owned_by) were correct; only created was absent. Routing proxies (LiteLLM, Portkey) use request-time unix_now() as the placeholder — there is no per-model creation timestamp in a routing proxy.
effect: 617 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Strict OpenAI SDK clients can now parse /v1/models responses without schema validation errors. The fix is request-time unix_now() (not a fixed epoch) because models are live at proxy-startup time and the client only needs a valid integer. No impact on routing, caching, auth, rate-limiting, or privacy paths.
grounding: ADR-171; OpenAI Model schema (created non-optional integer); IMP-8 (/v1/models endpoint parity); LiteLLM /v1/models response convention
risk: Low — additive field; no existing field changed; no behaviour change other than adding created to the JSON output; covered by a new schema-assertion test

title: calibrate warns when sample is too small for a reliable quantile (ADR-172)
change: cli.rs: added const MIN_CALIBRATE_SAMPLE: usize = 30 (with doc comment explaining the statistical basis). In run_calibrate, both the token-threshold branch and the logprob branch now check n < MIN_CALIBRATE_SAMPLE after computing the sample size and before printing the result; if true, they emit calibrate.small_sample via tf() with {n} and {min} placeholders. i18n.rs: added calibrate.small_sample key in EN ('  [note] {n} sample(s) is fewer than the recommended minimum ({min}). The quantile estimate has a wide confidence interval; collect more requests before relying on this recommendation.') and JA ('  [注] サンプル数 {n} 件は推奨最小値（{min}）を下回っています。分位点推定の信頼区間が広いため、この推奨値はリクエストが増えてから参照してください。').
reason: Socratic probe of the calibrate UX (IMP-2): a new user runs a handful of test requests and runs pasture calibrate. They see 'Calibrating threshold from 5 logged prompt(s)' and take the recommendation at face value. A quantile from n=5 has a 95% CI that spans nearly the whole sample range — at target=0.2, the recommended threshold could be anywhere from the 1st to the 5th sample, which might be a 10x range of token counts. Setting PASTURE_THRESHOLD from 5 data points is equivalent to setting it randomly. The command's prior UX implied reliability the math does not support for small n. The root defect: an advisory tool should surface when its advice is unreliable, not silently produce a number.
effect: 617 tests pass; clippy clean; zero new deps. Users with fewer than 30 logged requests see an advisory note between the header and the recommended threshold. The threshold is still printed (so new users can get started), but the uncertainty is stated explicitly. The calibration math is unchanged (calibrate.rs untouched). The warning triggers in both token-threshold and logprob modes. EN and JA strings added symmetrically.
grounding: ADR-172; IMP-2 (calibration command); RouterBench/UCCI sample-size notes; confidence-interval / small-sample advisory failure class
risk: Low — advisory text only; no change to calibration math, thresholds, routing, or any other behaviour; only the output is extended when n<30

title: Streaming backends use actual token counts from usage chunk, not estimates (ADR-173)
change: cloud.rs: (1) added Usage(u64,u64) variant to OpenAiStreamEvent; (2) extended parse_openai_stream_line to detect usage-only chunks (choices:[], usage:{prompt_tokens:N,completion_tokens:M}) and return Usage(p,c); (3) modified read_sse_body signature from Result<String,...> to Result<(String,Option<(u64,u64)>),...> to return usage alongside content; (4) extended emit_sse_lines to capture Usage events into a &mut Option<(u64,u64)>; (5) added stream_options:{include_usage:true} to build_body_stream; (6) updated HttpsCloudBackend::stream_complete to use captured usage with estimate_tokens fallback. backend.rs: updated HttpLocalBackend::stream_complete to match on both Delta and Usage events, capture usage, use it in the CompletionResponse with estimate_tokens fallback; build_body_stream already gained the stream_options flag. Tests: updated test_read_sse_body_openai to destructure (content, stream_usage) and assert stream_usage==None; added test_read_sse_body_openai_usage_chunk that sends a usage-only chunk and asserts stream_usage==Some((5,2)).
reason: Socratic probe of the streaming token-accounting path: both HttpLocalBackend::stream_complete (backend.rs) and HttpsCloudBackend::stream_complete (cloud.rs) called estimate_tokens for prompt_tokens and completion_tokens in the CompletionResponse, even though OpenAI-compatible backends send a final usage chunk (choices:[], usage:{prompt_tokens:N,completion_tokens:M}) when stream_options.include_usage:true is requested. Pasture was not requesting it and not parsing it, so every streaming request (local and cloud) logged estimated token counts to the cost log. This corrupted (1) the daily budget gauge (today_cloud_tokens, ADR-165/169), (2) cloud cost calculations (ADR-166), (3) the calibration data source (calibrate trains on prompt_tokens from the log, and streaming-heavy users got systematically biased estimates), and (4) the /metrics and /v1/stats endpoints that surface token totals. The estimate_tokens function is designed for pre-request routing decisions and leans high for budget safety — it is not a post-hoc reporting tool.
effect: 618 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. When the backend sends a usage chunk (OpenAI, LM Studio, Ollama with include_usage), the cost log, budget gauge, and /metrics/stats now record actual token counts. When it does not (older or non-compliant backends), estimate_tokens is used as before. The stream_options flag is added to all outgoing streaming requests; backends that do not support it ignore it (the field is part of the OpenAI spec and is safe to send). The change is correct even for the local backend because build_body_stream is used for both paths.
grounding: ADR-173; ADR-169 (budget gauge correctness); ADR-166 (cloud cost calculation); ADR-165 (budget observability); IMP-2 (calibrate trains on logged prompt_tokens); OpenAI streaming API stream_options.include_usage spec; actual-vs-estimated accounting failure class
risk: Low — outgoing requests gain one small field (stream_options.include_usage:true) which well-behaved backends ignore if unsupported; the estimate_tokens fallback preserves prior behaviour for backends that don't send usage chunks; the only observable change for compliant backends is that actual token counts replace estimates in the cost log and budget gauge

title: http_post_streaming checks HTTP status before emitting SSE lines (ADR-174)
change: backend.rs: http_post_streaming now parses the HTTP status code from the first header line after finding the CRLF-CRLF header terminator. If status is not 2xx, it reads the remainder of the body, takes up to 200 chars as a snippet, and returns crate::cloud::http_status_error(status, format!("HTTP {status}: {snippet}")) — the same helper read_sse_body uses — before calling on_line for any SSE content. The body bytes after the header terminator are accumulated into a separate vec for the error snippet. 618 tests pass.
reason: Socratic probe of the local-backend streaming path: http_post_streaming stripped the headers and called on_line for every body line without checking the HTTP status code. A 401 Unauthorized or 500 Internal Server Error from the local backend resulted in on_line being called with the error JSON (which parse_openai_stream_line silently returns None for), and the caller saw BackendError::Protocol('empty stream') — the empty-content guard in stream_complete — with no indication of the actual failure. The root defect was a parity gap with read_sse_body (the cloud streaming path), which has had a status check since it was introduced. The impact: an operator starting Pasture against a local backend that requires a different auth, or a backend that returns 422 for a malformed request, sees only 'empty stream' with no hint of what went wrong.
effect: 618 tests pass; clippy clean; zero new deps. Non-2xx responses from the local streaming path now produce a Transport (5xx) or Protocol (4xx) error with the HTTP status code and a body snippet, matching the cloud path. The same http_status_error retryability classification applies: 5xx triggers IMP-9 cloud_retry, 4xx propagates immediately. The on_line callback is never called for error responses. The change is a pure error-path improvement — the happy path is unchanged.
grounding: ADR-174; IMP-9 (transient-error retry, uses Transport vs Protocol classification); crate::cloud::http_status_error (the shared classifier); ADR-173 (the read_sse_body path that had the status check); silent-error / wrong-error failure class
risk: Low — the only changed behaviour is the error path: a non-2xx response now returns a named error instead of an empty-stream error; the happy path (2xx) is unchanged and tested; requires real TCP for direct unit testing (covered indirectly by the parallel read_sse_body tests which test the same http_status_error logic)

title: Anthropic streaming reports actual token counts (ADR-173 follow-up, ADR-175)
change: cloud.rs: parse_anthropic_stream_line now handles two new event types — message_start (extracts message.usage.input_tokens, emits Usage(input,0)) and message_delta (extracts usage.output_tokens, emits Usage(0,output)) — in addition to the existing content_block_delta and message_stop. Added a json_u64 helper to read JSON numbers as u64. emit_sse_lines now MERGES partial Usage events: a non-zero field overwrites the accumulated value, so OpenAI's single combined usage chunk and Anthropic's two split events both yield the correct (prompt,completion) pair. Tests: test_read_sse_body_anthropic_usage_split_across_events (full SSE body with message_start input=25 placeholder-output=1, content, message_delta output=42 → asserts (25,42) NOT (25,1)); test_anthropic_stream_line_usage_events (per-line: message_start→Usage(7,0), message_delta→Usage(0,13)).
reason: Socratic probe of the ADR-173 fix: ADR-173 made stream_complete use actual token counts from the usage chunk, but read_sse_body extracts usage via provider.parse_stream_line — and parse_anthropic_stream_line only recognised content_block_delta and message_stop. So for the Anthropic provider, no Usage event was ever emitted and stream_usage stayed None, falling back to estimate_tokens. The exact biased-accounting defect ADR-173 set out to fix (corrupt cost log, budget gauge, calibrate data) remained for every Anthropic streaming request. The fix was incomplete because it only addressed the OpenAI dialect. Anthropic's wire format differs: input_tokens is in message_start.message.usage, output_tokens is in the final message_delta.usage (the message_start output_tokens is a known placeholder of 1), so the counts arrive in separate events and must be merged.
effect: 620 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Anthropic cloud streaming now records actual prompt and completion tokens in the cost log, budget gauge (ADR-165/169), cloud cost (ADR-166), and /metrics + /v1/stats. The merge logic is dialect-agnostic: OpenAI sends one Usage(p,c); Anthropic sends Usage(input,0) then Usage(0,output); both converge to the correct pair. estimate_tokens fallback still applies if neither event carries usage (e.g. a truncated stream). The placeholder output_tokens=1 in message_start is correctly overwritten by the real value in message_delta.
grounding: ADR-175; ADR-173 (OpenAI streaming usage, the fix this completes); ADR-169/165 (budget gauge); ADR-166 (cloud cost); Anthropic Messages streaming API (message_start/message_delta usage split); incomplete-fix / provider-dialect-parity failure class
risk: Low — additive parsing of two Anthropic event types that were previously ignored (returned None); the merge logic preserves OpenAI behaviour exactly (single non-zero event sets both fields); covered by a full-body split-usage test and per-line parse tests; estimate_tokens fallback unchanged for the no-usage case

title: Explicit tool_choice:null no longer forces cloud escalation (ADR-176)
change: proxy.rs parse_request: tool_choice_active changed from `tc.as_str() != Some("none")` to `!matches!(tc, JsonValue::Null) && tc.as_str() != Some("none")`, so an explicit JSON null is treated like an absent field instead of an active tool choice. proxy_tests.rs: 2 new tests — test_tool_choice_null_does_not_escalate (bare tool_choice:null → has_tools false) and test_tool_choice_null_with_empty_tools_does_not_escalate (tools:[] + tool_choice:null, the realistic serializer shape → has_tools false).
reason: Socratic probe of the IMP-10 tool-routing signal: tool_choice_active was computed as tc.as_str() != Some("none"). JsonValue::Null.as_str() returns None, and None != Some("none") is true, so a request with "tool_choice": null set has_tools=true and was escalated to the cloud. Many OpenAI-compatible clients serialize every optional field including unset ones as null (Pydantic without exclude_none, several JS/TS SDKs, gRPC-JSON bridges), so this silently forced EVERY request from such a client to the cloud — the exact opposite of Pasture's privacy-first, local-first default. The user would see all traffic leaving their machine and all their cloud budget consumed, with no tools actually in play. The defect: the null case (explicit 'no value') was conflated with the named-object case (a real tool choice) because both fail the as_str()=='none' check.
effect: 622 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. A null tool_choice now behaves exactly like an absent one — the request routes by its content/length signals as normal, staying local when appropriate. Genuine tool signals are unaffected: a non-empty tools/functions array, tool_choice:"auto"/"required", and named-function objects all still set has_tools and escalate. Only tool_choice:"none" and tool_choice:null keep the request eligible for local routing. Privacy-first default restored for clients that emit null fields.
grounding: ADR-176; IMP-10 (tool/function-calling escalation signal); privacy-first local-first routing default (ADR-007/IMP-3); null-vs-absent JSON conflation failure class
risk: Low — narrows the escalation trigger to exclude only the JSON null case; every genuine tool signal (arrays, auto/required, named objects) is unchanged and still tested; the change is one boolean guard with direct unit coverage proving null stays local while the existing auto/required/named/none tests prove the other cases are preserved

title: Tool/function definitions forwarded to the backend — IMP-10 completed (ADR-177)
change: backend.rs: SamplingParams gained tools:Option<JsonValue> and tool_choice:Option<JsonValue> (stored beside response_format so no request-construction site changes); openai_fields() now appends ,"tools":... and ,"tool_choice":... when present; new ollama_tools_field() forwards tools (not tool_choice) into OllamaBackend::build_body_inner. CompletionResponse gained tool_calls:Option<String> (raw array) and now derives Default. cloud.rs: Provider::parse_response signature changed to return (content, tool_calls, p, c); the OpenAI branch extracts choices[0].message.tool_calls and only errors when neither content nor tool_calls is present (a tool call has content:null); the Anthropic branch returns None (follow-up). proxy.rs: parse_sampling captures tools (non-empty array only) and tool_choice (non-null only); build_openai_response_with_injection emits ,"tool_calls":... and finish_reason:"tool_calls" when present. cache.rs: hash_sampling folds tools/tool_choice into the key so different tools never cross-serve. Construction sites for CompletionResponse updated across backend.rs, cloud.rs, cache.rs, proxy_tests.rs. Tests: 7 new (openai_fields forwards tools+tool_choice; Ollama forwards tools and omits tool_choice; parse_response surfaces tool_calls; build_openai_response emits tool_calls+finish_reason; ordinary response stays stop; tools change the cache key; parse_request captures/omits tools).
reason: Socratic probe of the IMP-10 promise ('detect tools/tool_choice -> escalate AND pass through unchanged'): CompletionRequest stored only has_tools:bool. Neither build_body_inner (Ollama) nor build_body_opts (OpenAI/Anthropic) forwarded the tools array, so the tool definitions were silently dropped. Pasture escalated tool requests to the stronger model (correct routing) but then stripped the payload, so the model never saw the tools and could not emit a tool call. Compounding it, parse_response required choices[0].message.content, which is null for a tool-call response, so even a correct upstream tool response would have errored with 'missing content'. The feature was half-implemented: the routing signal existed without the forwarding or the response handling. For any client doing function calling through Pasture (the common agent/tool-use case), tool calls were impossible.
effect: 630 tests pass (7 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. On the OpenAI-compatible path (cloud OpenAI provider, local OpenAI-compatible backend via Provider::OpenAI.build_body, and Ollama /api/chat) tool definitions now reach the model and tool_calls responses are surfaced to the client with the correct finish_reason. The cache key distinguishes tool sets. Empty tools / null tool_choice are not forwarded (nothing to carry; consistent with ADR-176). Anthropic tool-use (different tools schema + tool_use blocks) and streaming tool-call deltas are explicitly out of scope and fall back to prior behaviour — documented as the next steps.
grounding: ADR-177; IMP-10 (tool/function-calling escalation signal, the promise this completes); ADR-176 (tool_choice null handling); response_format passthrough precedent (the SamplingParams pattern reused); ADR-158/159 (cache key includes output-affecting fields); OpenAI tool-calling / Chat Completions tool_calls schema; half-built-feature failure class
risk: Medium — touches the core request body builders, the response parser, and the response builder. Mitigations: the OpenAI parse_response now errors only when BOTH content and tool_calls are absent (strictly more permissive than before — every previously-valid response still parses), forwarding is additive (absent tools change nothing), and the change is covered by 7 new tests plus the full existing suite (623->630) which exercises the unchanged text-completion path. Anthropic and streaming are deliberately unchanged to bound the blast radius.

title: Streaming responses carry tool_calls — ADR-177 follow-up (ADR-178)
change: cloud.rs: new OpenAiStreamEvent::ToolCallDelta(String) variant; parse_openai_stream_line detects delta.tool_calls (non-empty array) and returns the raw fragment. New ToolCallAccumulator (push(delta_json) merges fragments by index — id/type/function.name set from first non-empty fragment, function.arguments concatenated; finish() builds the complete tool_calls array string). read_sse_body return type changed from (String,Option<(u64,u64)>) to a new SseStreamResult{content,usage,tool_calls} struct; emit_sse_lines gained a &mut ToolCallAccumulator and a ToolCallDelta arm; the empty-stream guard now passes when content is empty but tool_calls is Some. reason: Socratic probe of the multi-turn tool-calling path: 'the tool-calling loop has a second turn — the client sends a role:tool result message with tool_call_id. What does Pasture do with it?' title: Token estimation counts tool definitions and tool_calls payloads (ADR-184)
change: backend.rs: new CompletionRequest::estimation_text() = routing_text() + serialised sampling.tools + sampling.tool_choice + every assistant message's tool_calls_json. The five token-ACCOUNTING sites switched from routing_text() to estimation_text(): OllamaBackend::complete (prompt-token fallback), OllamaBackend::stream_complete fallback, HttpLocalBackend(OpenAI-compat)::stream_complete fallback, HttpsCloudBackend::stream_complete fallback (cloud.rs), and apply_budget_guard's estimate_total_tokens pre-reservation (proxy.rs). The routing-DECISION and privacy sites (classify, decide, the injection guard) keep routing_text() unchanged. Also cleaned three pre-existing clippy warnings introduced by ADR-181 (finish_reason_for(&hit)/(&r) double-ref, a test remove_file(&otel) needless borrow). 1 new test (estimation_text includes tools+tool_calls and exceeds routing_text; plain request unchanged). 659 total.
reason: Socratic probe of the ADR-177..183 tool-calling series from the cost/budget angle: 'when a backend sends no usage chunk, what token count does a tool-heavy request log?' routing_text() joins only message content, so the tools array (often hundreds of tokens of JSON schema), the tool_choice, and the assistant tool_calls arguments were all excluded from the estimate. Those bytes are really serialised into the request body and billed by the provider, so the cost log, the daily budget gauge/cap (IMP-26/ADR-165/169), the spike detector, and cloud cost (ADR-166) all systematically UNDER-counted tool-calling requests on the estimate-fallback path — the unsafe direction for a budget control (under-enforcement) and a silent under-report for spend. routing_text() itself must stay content-only: it also feeds privacy classify() (which must see only user-visible text) and the routing decision (where tool presence already forces escalation via has_tools, so tool tokens would be redundant). The fix is therefore a separate estimation_text() used only at the accounting sites, not a change to routing_text().
effect: 659 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean (also fixed 3 pre-existing ADR-181 lint warnings); zero new deps. Tool definitions, tool_choice, and assistant tool_calls now count toward the estimated prompt tokens used for the cost log and budget/spike guard when the backend returns no actual usage chunk. The actual-usage path (ADR-173/175) is unaffected — actual counts still take precedence; this only improves the fallback estimate. Routing and privacy behaviour is byte-identical (routing_text() unchanged at those sites). The MockBackend test helper keeps routing_text() (test-only, not a billing path).
grounding: ADR-184; ADR-177..183 (tool-calling series, documented this as the follow-up); IMP-26 (budget/spike guard under-count); ADR-165/169 (budget gauge); ADR-166 (cloud cost); ADR-173/175 (actual-usage path that this fallback complements); under-count / control-under-enforcement failure class
risk: Low — additive estimate refinement on the fallback path only; actual-usage counts still take precedence; routing/privacy sites untouched (routing_text() unchanged); over-counting is impossible (only adds real request bytes) and under-counting is reduced; covered by a new test plus full regression

title: Spike-detector running average resets on UTC day rollover (ADR-185)
change: proxy.rs roll_budget_day_if_needed(): when the UTC day strictly advances and the CAS wins, the function already zeroed today_cloud_tokens; it now also zeroes cloud_token_sum and cloud_request_count. These two counters back the spike detector's running average (avg = cloud_token_sum / cloud_request_count in check_budget_and_spike). 1 new test (test_spike_counters_reset_on_day_rollover: seed stale lifetime totals, anchor budget_day to the past, issue a cloud request, assert the spike counters were reset to this-request-only values). 660 total.
reason: Socratic probe of the IMP-26 budget/spike guard from the long-running-process angle: 'the daily token budget resets at UTC midnight (ADR-155), but does the spike detector's average reset with it?' It did not. cloud_token_sum and cloud_request_count accumulated for the entire lifetime of the process, so the spike detector compared each request against an all-time average rather than a recent one. Two failure modes: (1) the average is dominated by stale history and never decays — a few early outliers permanently skew it, and a genuinely large-but-legitimate prompt late in a long session may never trip the spike because the lifetime average has drifted high; (2) symmetrically, a long quiet history of small requests pins the average low so the detector becomes hair-trigger. The daily budget is already day-scoped (ADR-155); the spike average should share the same window so the two halves of the IMP-26 guard age consistently. Resetting on the same rollover the budget uses keeps it simple, deterministic, and std-only (no rolling-window ring buffer or EWMA state needed).
effect: 660 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. The spike detector now compares each request against the current UTC day's running average instead of an all-time average, so it stays responsive to genuine spikes in a long-running process and is not skewed by stale early-session outliers. Same-day behaviour is unchanged (the reset only fires on a strict day advance, gated by the existing ADR-155 CAS, so a backward clock still cannot reset it). The budget counter and the spike counters now reset together on the same rollover.
grounding: ADR-185; IMP-26 (budget/spike guard); ADR-155 (UTC day rollover reset, backward-clock-safe CAS — reused as the single reset point); ADR-184 (the estimation_text feeding this average); stale-statistic / non-decaying-average failure class

title: Exact-match cache key includes message-level tool_calls / tool_call_id (ADR-186)
change: cache.rs request_key(): the per-message hash now folds in m.tool_call_id and m.tool_calls_json alongside m.role and m.content.trim(). Structured tool fields are hashed exactly (no whitespace normalisation). 1 new test (test_request_key_distinguishes_tool_calls_and_id: book(NYC) vs book(LON) tool_calls produce distinct keys; differing tool_call_id produces distinct keys; identical tool_calls stay stable). 661 total.
reason: Socratic probe of the ADR-177..185 tool-calling series from the cache lens: 'ADR-177 put sampling-level tools/tool_choice in the cache key — but ADR-182/183 added message-level tool_call_id and tool_calls_json. Are those in the key too?' They were not. request_key() hashed only m.role and m.content.trim() per message, so two multi-turn histories with identical message content but different assistant tool_calls — e.g. an assistant turn calling book(to:NYC) vs book(to:LON), each followed by the same tool-result content and the same user follow-up — collided to the same key. The second conversation would be served the first conversation's cached completion: a wrong, potentially cross-user answer that may reference the wrong tool arguments. tool_call_id is likewise significant (it binds a tool result to a specific call). The cache is reached for tool-calling requests because has_tools does not make a request sensitive — sensitivity comes from classify(routing_text()), which is content-only — so non-sensitive-content tool requests ARE cached. This is the exact failure class ADR-177 fixed at the sampling level, missed at the message level when ADR-182/183 introduced the new fields.
effect: 661 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Multi-turn tool-calling conversations can no longer cross-serve a cached response when only the tool_calls arguments or tool_call_id differ. Plain (non-tool) requests are byte-identical in behaviour: both new fields are None for them, so the hash is unchanged and all existing cache keys/tests are stable. The semantic-cache sampling_key path (ADR-159) is unaffected — it already hashed sampling-level tools/tool_choice via hash_sampling; this fix is specifically the message-level fields the exact-match key iterates.
grounding: ADR-186; ADR-177 (sampling-level tools/tool_choice in the cache key — the same invariant at a different level); ADR-182 (tool_call_id field); ADR-183 (tool_calls_json field); ADR-159 (sampling_key / semantic cache, confirmed unaffected); cache-collision / stale-cross-serve failure class
risk: Low — the change only ADDS two fields to an existing hash; it cannot merge previously-distinct keys (only split previously-colliding ones), so no valid cache hit is lost and no stale entry is newly served. For all non-tool requests both fields are None and the key is unchanged (verified by the unmodified whitespace/stable/distinct tests). Covered by a new targeted test plus the full regression suite (660->661).

title: Privacy classifier scans tool-call arguments, not just message content (ADR-187)
change: backend.rs: new CompletionRequest::privacy_text() = routing_text() + every assistant message's tool_calls_json (the model-generated tool-call arguments). proxy.rs classify_and_decide(): classify() now runs on req.privacy_text() instead of routing_text(); the routing *difficulty* decision passed to decide_full still uses content-only routing_text() so tool bytes don't inflate the token-length heuristic. Tool *definitions* (sampling.tools) are intentionally excluded from privacy_text() to avoid false-positive sensitivity on developer-authored schema. 2 new tests (backend: privacy_text includes tool-call args, excludes tool defs, and makes a card-in-arguments request classify sensitive; proxy: a credit card living only in tool_calls_json keeps an otherwise-cloud-bound request local). 663 total.
reason: Socratic probe surfaced at the end of ADR-186: 'ADR-186 confirmed tool-calling requests ARE cached and routed because sensitivity comes from classify(routing_text()), which is content-only. So where does sensitive data in a tool-call argument get classified?' Nowhere. routing_text() joins only message content, so PII that lives solely in an assistant message's tool_calls_json (e.g. a credit-card number the model passed to a charge_card tool, or an email/API key in tool arguments) was invisible to classify(). The request would then be classified non-sensitive, and because has_tools is a hard escalation signal (and long content escalates on length), it would route to CLOUD — leaking the PII off the machine. This directly violates the project's preserved security guarantee: sensitive content must NOT leave the machine unless PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD is set. ADR-184 had explicitly noted routing_text() must stay content-only for classify() 'user-visible text only' — but that reasoning missed that tool_calls_json is also outbound request data that can carry conversation-derived PII; estimation_text() already counted those bytes for billing, yet classify() never saw them for privacy. The fix gives privacy its own text (privacy_text) that includes tool-call arguments, parallel to how estimation_text() serves token-counting — three purpose-built projections of the request (routing_text=decision/length, estimation_text=billing, privacy_text=PII classification).
effect: 663 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. A credit card, email, API key, JWT, or any other classifier category appearing only in a tool-call argument now marks the request sensitive, so it is kept local (and, via the same sensitive flag, not cached — closing the cache side too). The routing difficulty/length decision is byte-identical (still routing_text()), so non-PII tool requests route exactly as before. Tool definitions are excluded by design, so merely declaring a tool whose description mentions a keyword does not force a request local. Both the buffered and streaming paths are covered because both go through classify_and_decide.

title: Pseudonymizer scrubs PII in tool-call argument JSON strings (ADR-188)
change: pseudonymize.rs: new replace_in_json_strings(json, ctx) function — walks every JSON string literal in the input, decodes the escape sequences (\" -> ", \\ -> \, etc.), recursively calls itself when the decoded value looks like a JSON object/array (handling the tool-call `arguments` field which is itself JSON-encoded JSON), and applies replace_in_text to plain string values; re-encodes with crate::json::escape_string. pseudonymize_messages: tool_calls_json is now passed through replace_in_json_strings (previously cloned unchanged with an incorrect comment). 5 new tests (email in compact JSON args; IP in compact JSON args; token maps back via restore(); benign args unchanged; same value in content + args shares a stable token). 668 total.
reason: Socratic probe of the ADR-188 pseudonymizer path: 'ADR-187 added privacy_text() so that PII in tool_calls_json keeps the request local in the DEFAULT case. But when PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD + PASTURE_PSEUDONYMIZE are both set (the opted-in masked-cloud mode), the pseudonymizer fires. Does it scrub PII in tool_calls_json before the request leaves?' It did not. pseudonymize_messages only applied replace_in_text to m.content; tool_calls_json was cloned unchanged, with a comment that it 'does not need pseudonymization' — a comment that was written before ADR-182/183 established that tool arguments can carry PII, and that ADR-187 invalidated. Even if it had tried to use replace_in_text directly on the raw tool_calls_json string, it would have failed: replace_in_text is a whitespace tokenizer, and inside compact JSON strings like {"email":"alice@example.com"} there is no whitespace to split on — alice@example.com is part of a single large token surrounded by {"email":" and "}, so the email detector never fires. A JSON-string-aware walker is necessary. The implementation recursively descends: the outer tool_calls_json is walked for JSON string literals; the `arguments` field (itself a JSON-encoded string) is detected as starting with `{` or `[` and recursed into; the innermost string values ("alice@example.com") are decoded and processed by replace_in_text where they are now standalone whitespace tokens. The shared-token property (same PII in content and args gets the same token) is a natural consequence of sharing a single ctx across the entire message.
effect: 668 tests pass (5 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. In PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD + PASTURE_PSEUDONYMIZE mode, PII appearing only in tool-call argument JSON is now replaced with stable tokens before the request leaves, and restored from the mapping after the cloud response arrives. The default case (sensitive content kept local, no cloud at all) is unchanged — this only affects the opted-in masked-cloud path. Benign tool-call arguments (no PII) are re-encoded identically (tested). The JSON re-encoding via escape_string is deterministic and round-trips through the JSON parser correctly.
grounding: ADR-188; ADR-187 (privacy_text — the classification side of this same blind spot); ADR-182/183 (tool_call_id / tool_calls_json fields — established that these can carry PII); IMP-19 (pseudonymization); PII-bypass / masked-cloud-leakage failure class
risk: Low. The change only fires when PASTURE_PSEUDONYMIZE=1 and the route is Cloud — a deliberately opted-in path. The JSON walker only modifies string values that match PII patterns; all other content passes through verbatim. Re-encoding is via the existing escape_string (already tested by the json module). Benign arguments are unchanged (tested). The five new tests cover the critical paths: email + IP detection in compact JSON, restore round-trip, shared token across content+args, and the benign no-op case.

title: Pseudonymize restore covers cloud-generated tool_calls in the response (ADR-189)
change: proxy.rs buffered path (run_completion): after restoring resp.content, also restores resp.tool_calls with the same mapping when it is Some and the mapping is non-empty. proxy.rs streaming path (stream_chat_to_socket): before emitting the accumulated tool_calls as an SSE delta chunk, restores tokens using cache_mapping (the Mapping clone already kept for cache restoration, parallel to the StreamRestorer used for text deltas). 2 new tests (buffered: ToolCallReplyBackend returns tool_calls with <EMAIL_1> token, verify it becomes alice@example.com in the response JSON; streaming: same backend with stream:true, verify the SSE output contains the restored value). 670 total.
reason: Socratic probe of ADR-188's restore path: 'ADR-188 pseudonymizes outbound tool_calls_json (history). But when the cloud model RESPONDS with its own tool call that echoes a pseudonymized token it saw in the history — e.g. <EMAIL_1> appeared in the request context and the cloud model uses it in its response tool call — does restore() de-anonymize it?' It did not. The buffered path (line 1519) restored resp.content but not resp.tool_calls; the streaming path emitted the tool_calls SSE chunk (line 2522-2528) also without restoration. This means the raw <EMAIL_1> token (or <IP_1>, <PHONE_1>, etc.) was forwarded verbatim to the client in the tool_calls field — the client code calling the API would see opaque tokens instead of the real values, breaking any workflow that uses the tool_call arguments. The mapping was available on both paths (pseudo_mapping in the buffered path; cache_mapping on the streaming path), so the fix is two targeted one-liner-style additions. The streaming path already had cache_mapping as a separate Mapping clone (kept for cache restoration, ADR-147), so no new state was needed.
effect: 670 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. In masked-cloud mode (PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD + PASTURE_PSEUDONYMIZE), if the cloud responds with tool_calls that contain pseudonymized tokens, those tokens are now de-anonymized before the response reaches the client — matching the already-correct behavior for resp.content. Both buffered and streaming paths are covered. Non-pseudonymized requests are unaffected (both new branches gate on an existing mapping, short-circuit on empty/None).
grounding: ADR-189; ADR-188 (pseudonymize outbound tool_calls_json — the inbound counterpart); IMP-19 (pseudonymization); ADR-147 (cache_mapping clone on the streaming path — reused for this fix); ADR-178 (streaming tool_calls chunk emission — the site being fixed); pseudonymization-incomplete / token-leakage failure class
risk: Low. The changes are additive on paths already gated by an existing non-empty mapping check. resp.tool_calls restoration uses the same restore() call already used for resp.content (no new code path). The streaming restoration uses cache_mapping, a Mapping clone already maintained on this path for cache purposes — no new state or ownership change. Covered by 2 new targeted tests plus full regression.

title: SPEC.md / config drift-guard test + spec brought current through ADR-189 (ADR-190)
change: SPEC.md: updated to current implementation — added 21 missing PASTURE_* env vars to the §8 config table (budget/spike, pseudonymize, injection guard, semantic cache, cache TTL/control, access/otel logs, hard-prompts, skills, system prompt, local timeout, max body bytes, cloud price, fallback provider/model, state, donate); fixed the PASTURE_PROXY_TOKEN -> PASTURE_AUTH_TOKEN error and the phantom per-input/output price vars (actual: single PASTURE_CLOUD_PRICE_PER_1M); added §4 'three request projections' (routing_text/estimation_text/privacy_text); added §7.1 budget+spike guard, §7.2 injection guard, §9.1 OTel trace log, §12 tool/function-calling (ADR-177..189), §13 reversible pseudonymization; refreshed §2 CLI table and §14 conformance. config.rs: 2 new tests — test_spec_documents_every_env_var_config_reads (every std::env::var("PASTURE_*") literal in config.rs must appear in a SPEC.md config-table row) and test_spec_has_no_phantom_pasture_env_vars (no table row may name a PASTURE_* var config.rs never reads, allow-listing BYOK keys / referral / PASTURE_LANG resolved outside config.rs). 672 total.
reason: User asked to author/refresh the specification and to enumerate strengths/weaknesses/improvements and implement. Surveying the spec against the code revealed substantial drift: SPEC.md tracked ADRs only through ~136, omitted 21 environment variables the config layer actually reads, referenced a non-existent PASTURE_PROXY_TOKEN (the real var is PASTURE_AUTH_TOKEN), and invented per-input/per-output price vars that do not exist. Writing the test immediately paid off: it caught four further gaps in the hand-updated spec (PASTURE_OLLAMA_PORT written as shorthand _PORT, PASTURE_CLOUD_FALLBACK_PROVIDER/MODEL documented only in prose not the table, and a duplicated PASTURE_CLOUD_MODEL row).
effect: 672 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. SPEC.md is now normative and current through ADR-189, and any future change that adds/renames a PASTURE_* env var without updating the SPEC.md table (or vice versa) fails CI. The guard is std-only: it reads config.rs via include_str! and SPEC.md via CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR at test time, with no runtime cost and no effect on the shipped binary.
grounding: ADR-190; the i18n EN/JA key-parity test (the existing parity-test convention this mirrors); SPEC.md §8 config table; ADR-177..189 (the series the spec now documents in §12/§13); documentation-drift / spec-implementation-divergence failure class

title: Injection-guard flag mode annotates the streaming response, not just buffered (ADR-191)
change: proxy.rs: new build_openai_injection_chunk() emits a leading chat.completion.chunk with an empty delta and a top-level x_pasture_injection_flag field (alongside the existing x_pasture_route). stream_chat_to_socket: the streaming injection guard now captures the flag label into injection_label: Option<String> (was a bare eprintln!) and emits the leading flag chunk as the first SSE data frame on every emission path. write_cached_stream gained an injection_label: Option<&str> parameter and emits the flag chunk too, so a flagged cache/semantic-cache hit is annotated as well; both call sites pass injection_label.as_deref(). The main backend-stream path emits it right after the shared id/model/created are set. 2 new tests (streaming flag mode surfaces x_pasture_injection_flag; benign streaming request is not flagged). 674 total.
reason: Socratic probe of the injection guard (IMP-20) for buffered/streaming parity, the same asymmetry class the project has repeatedly closed (ADR-147 cache, ADR-149 framing, ADR-189 tool_calls restore): 'the buffered path annotates a flagged request with x_pasture_injection_flag in the response JSON (complete_buffered -> build_openai_response_with_injection), and SPEC.md 7.2 says flag mode annotates the response — does the streaming path do the same?' It did not. The streaming guard only did eprintln! and the code comment claimed it 'cannot annotate mid-stream chunks' — but streaming chunks already carry a non-standard top-level x_pasture_route field, so a x_pasture_injection_flag field is equally feasible. The result was that a streaming client in flag mode could not distinguish a flagged request from a clean one, while a buffered client could — a silent behavioural divergence and a mismatch with the spec written in ADR-190. block mode was already correct in both paths (rejects before the stream starts); only the advisory flag annotation was missing on the stream.
effect: 674 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Streaming flag-mode requests now emit a leading SSE chunk carrying x_pasture_injection_flag:<label>, so a client gets the same signal whether or not it set stream:true, on the backend-stream, exact-cache, and semantic-cache paths. SPEC.md 7.2 ('flag annotates the response with x_pasture_injection_flag and proceeds') is now true for both paths without any spec change. Buffered behaviour is byte-identical. Off and block modes are unchanged.
grounding: ADR-191; IMP-20 (injection guard); ADR-190 (SPEC.md 7.2 which this makes accurate for streaming); ADR-147/149/189 (the buffered/streaming-parity series this continues); build_openai_response_with_injection (the buffered annotation this mirrors); streaming/buffered-divergence failure class

The leading empty-delta chunk is a valid OpenAI chat.completion.chunk shape; clients that ignore unknown top-level fields (as they must for x_pasture_route already) are unaffected. write_cached_stream's new parameter is threaded through both existing call sites.
