title: Access log records the real HTTP status for rejected streaming requests (ADR-192)
change: proxy.rs: stream_chat_to_socket now returns std::io::Result<u16> (the effective HTTP status) instead of Result<()>. Each pre-stream rejection path returns its real status: injection block -> 400; classify_and_decide / apply_budget_guard / backend_for errors -> e.status() (429/502/503); exact- and semantic-cache hits and the normal stream -> 200. The HTTP dispatch loop previously called access_log!(200u16) unconditionally before invoking the streaming handler; it now logs the status the handler returns (Ok(status)), and on a mid-stream io error still logs 200 (the SSE headers were already sent) before propagating the error. 2 new tests (a stream:true injection-block request is access-logged as 400; a normal stream is still logged as 200). 676 total.
reason: Socratic probe of the access log (IMP-access-log) for buffered/streaming parity, continuing the observability lens from ADR-191: 'the buffered path logs the actual response status via the wr!/wr_result! macros, but the streaming branch calls access_log!(200u16) BEFORE stream_chat_to_socket runs, with the comment SSE header sent before streaming; log TTFB. Is that 200 always correct?' No. stream_chat_to_socket has four pre-stream rejection paths that write a non-200 status to the socket and return: injection-guard block (400), routing error (503/502), budget block (429), and backend-unavailable (502/503). In every one of those cases the client received an error but the access log recorded 200 — a silent observability defect that would hide guard/budget rejections of streaming clients from anyone auditing the access log (e.g. to spot abuse or misconfiguration). The buffered path never had this problem because its status flows through the wr! macros. The 200-before-streaming shortcut assumed a stream always starts with 200 SSE headers, which is false when a pre-flight check rejects first.
effect: 676 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. The access log now reflects the status the streaming client actually received: 400 for an injection block, 429 for a budget block, 502/503 for routing/backend errors, and 200 for a started stream (including cache replays). A mid-stream client disconnect is still logged as 200 (the headers were sent), matching prior behaviour. The logged duration for a successful stream is now the full request time rather than the near-zero pre-stream time, which is strictly more useful for latency auditing. Buffered logging is unchanged.
grounding: ADR-192; IMP-access-log; ADR-191 (the immediately preceding buffered/streaming observability-parity fix); IMP-20 (injection block, one of the mislogged rejections); IMP-26 (budget block, another); observability/wrong-status-logging failure class
risk: Low. The status-returning refactor is mechanical: every existing return path now yields a status, the success/cache paths return 200 (identical client bytes), and the rejection paths return the same status they already wrote to the socket. The only behavioural change is the access-log status/duration for streaming requests, which moves from always-200/pre-stream-time to actual-status/full-duration. Mid-stream io errors are explicitly still logged as 200 to match the bytes already sent. Covered by 2 new tests (rejection logs 400, success logs 200) plus the full regression (674->676).

title: OTel error spans for budget-block and backend-unavailable rejections (ADR-193)
change: proxy.rs: new emit_error_span(&mut otel_span, route, error) helper centralises the status=error + message + route + system + finish + append sequence (ADR-143). Refactored the two existing duplicated error-span blocks (buffered backend-failure in run_completion; streaming backend-failure in stream_chat_to_socket) to call it. Added error-span emission at three rejection points that previously dropped a started span: buffered budget block (converted apply_budget_guard's `?` shortcut into a match that emits the span then returns Err), streaming budget block, and streaming backend-unavailable early returns. 2 new tests (buffered budget block emits status:error span; streaming budget block emits status:error span and returns 429). 678 total.
reason: Socratic probe continuing the observability lens from ADR-191/192: 'ADR-143 emits an OTel error span when a backend FAILS, but does a request that is REJECTED after the span is started also get traced, or is the span silently dropped?' Tracing the span lifecycle showed the OTel span is started early (buffered run_completion line 1431; streaming line 2387) but three rejection paths returned without finalising it: (1) the buffered budget block used self.apply_budget_guard(req, planned_route)? — the ? propagated the BudgetExceeded error past the only error-span block (which sat in the later completion_result match), so the started span vanished; (2) the streaming budget-block early return and (3) the streaming backend-unavailable early return both write the HTTP error and return without touching otel_span. Net effect: a 429 budget rejection was invisible in the trace log on both paths, and a 502/503 backend-unavailable was invisible on the streaming path — exactly the silent-drop ADR-143 set out to prevent, just at a different point in the request. Only buffered backend-unavailable was already traced (via the completion_result error arm). The fix unifies all rejection/failure paths on one emit_error_span helper so a started span is always finalised — as an error when the request fails or is rejected, as a normal span on success.
effect: 678 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Budget-block (429) rejections now appear in the OTel trace log with status:error and a pasture.error attribute on both the buffered and streaming paths; streaming backend-unavailable (502/503) rejections are now traced too. The new helper removes ~20 lines of duplicated span-emission code across two sites. Success spans, cache-hit spans (ADR-144), and the buffered backend-failure span are unchanged in behaviour (the latter two now route through the same helper / unchanged code). Tracing remains a no-op when PASTURE_OTEL_LOG is unset.
grounding: ADR-193; ADR-143 (error spans for backend failures — the principle this extends to rejections); ADR-144 (cache-hit spans, the early-span-start this depends on); ADR-191/192 (the buffered/streaming observability-parity series this continues); IMP-26 (budget block, the main newly-traced rejection); IMP-23 (OTel trace log); silently-dropped-span / observability-gap failure class
risk: Low. emit_error_span is a no-op when tracing is off or no span exists, so default builds are unaffected. The two refactored blocks produce byte-identical span output (same fields, same order). The three new emission points each fire immediately before an early return that already writes the client error, so they add a trace line without changing the response. The buffered budget-block change converts a `?` into an equivalent match (Ok path identical; Err path emits then returns the same error). Covered by 2 new tests plus the full regression (676->678).

title: Release budget pre-reservation when a buffered cloud completion fails (ADR-194)
change: proxy.rs run_completion: the completion_result Err arm now calls release_cloud_tokens(budget_reserved_outer) before returning the error, mirroring the streaming path's existing rollback. proxy.rs stream_chat_to_socket: the backend-unavailable early return also releases budget_reserved defensively (invariant: every early return after apply_budget_guard reserved tokens must roll them back). 1 new test (a cloud completion that fails with no local fallback under an active budget must leave today_cloud_tokens at its pre-request value, not inflated by the phantom reservation). 679 total.
reason: Socratic probe continuing the rejection-path consistency lens (ADR-192/193): 'apply_budget_guard pre-reserves estimated tokens on the today_cloud_tokens gauge (ADR-163); the success path reconciles via log_cost and the fallback-to-local path releases in log_cost — but what happens to the reservation when the cloud completion fails ENTIRELY (cloud + fallback both fail, no local)?' The buffered run_completion error arm (the same arm ADR-143/193 use to emit the error span) returned Err WITHOUT releasing budget_reserved_outer, so the estimated tokens of a request that never completed stayed on the daily gauge permanently. Over many transient cloud failures the gauge would drift upward and eventually block the cloud route for the rest of the UTC day (until the midnight roll), a self-inflicted denial of the cloud backend. The streaming path already released on backend failure (ADR-163, the Err arm of stream_complete), so this was a buffered/streaming asymmetry AND a real leak. Confirmed by temporarily disabling the fix: the gauge was left at 17 (the estimate for a one-token request) instead of 0. Also hardened the streaming backend-unavailable early return (added by ADR-193) with the same release, upholding the invariant that every post-reservation early return rolls back.
effect: 679 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. A buffered cloud completion that fails with no local fallback now releases its budget pre-reservation, keeping the today_cloud_tokens gauge (/metrics, /v1/stats, and the budget enforcer) accurate across transient cloud outages — no phantom accumulation, no eventual self-block. Successful completions, fallback-to-local (released in log_cost), and budget-block rejections (no reservation made under block action) are unchanged. The streaming path's behaviour is unchanged in the reachable cases and now also correct in the defensive backend-unavailable case.
grounding: ADR-194; ADR-163 (atomic budget pre-reservation and its rollback contract — this closes a gap in it); ADR-164 (saturating release across day rollover, reused here); ADR-169 (reserved=0 under spike-only so no double-release); ADR-192/193 (the rejection-path consistency series this continues); IMP-26 (budget guard); phantom-reservation / resource-leak failure class
risk: Low. The fix only adds a release on an error path that currently leaks; release_cloud_tokens saturates at 0 (ADR-164) so it cannot underflow even across a UTC day rollover between reservation and failure. budget_reserved_outer is non-zero only when the daily budget is active and the route was cloud, exactly the case that reserved tokens; in all other cases it is 0 and the release is a no-op. The streaming addition guards a path where the reservation is ~always 0 (route=cloud implies a cloud backend), so it is defensive. Covered by a new test that fails without the fix (gauge=17) and passes with it (gauge=0), plus the full regression (678->679).

title: Cost-log summary counts semantic-cache hits in the cache bucket (ADR-195)
change: cost.rs fold_record: the route match arm `"cache" => s.cache += 1` became `"cache" | "semantic_cache" => s.cache += 1`, so a semantic-cache hit (logged with route="semantic_cache", ADR-150) counts toward the cache bucket like an exact-match hit. 1 new test (a mix of cache + semantic_cache + cloud + local: cache==2, local+cloud+cache==total, cache_rate==0.5). 680 total.
reason: Socratic probe of the cost-log aggregation feeding stats / /v1/stats / /metrics (the observability surface ADR-192/193 touched): 'fold_record increments total for every record but buckets only local/cloud/cache — what route labels actually get logged?' The semantic cache returns route_label="semantic_cache" on both the buffered path (run_completion line 1479: Ok((hit, "semantic_cache", None, 0))) and the streaming path (write_cached_stream with "semantic_cache"), and log_cost writes route="semantic_cache" to the cost log. But fold_record's match had no arm for it, so it fell through `_ => {}`: a semantic-cache hit incremented total without landing in local, cloud, OR cache. Consequences: (1) the invariant total = local + cloud + cache silently broke whenever the semantic cache (PASTURE_SEMANTIC_CACHE, IMP-12) was enabled and hit; (2) cache_rate = cache/total undercounted true cache effectiveness (semantic hits in the denominator but missing from the numerator), understating exactly the feature a user enabled the semantic cache to get; (3) stats/-/v1/stats/-/metrics presented an inconsistent picture where the route counts did not sum to the total. A semantic-cache hit is a cache hit by every meaningful definition — no backend call, zero cost — so it belongs in the cache bucket. fold_record is shared by summarize (whole-slice, pasture stats) and the proxy's incremental metrics cache (IMP-32/ADR-151), so the one-line fix corrects every consumer at once.
effect: 680 tests pass (1 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. With the semantic cache enabled, pasture stats, GET /v1/stats, and GET /metrics now report cache hits that include semantic hits, the invariant total = local + cloud + cache holds again, and cache_rate reflects true cache effectiveness. Deployments without the semantic cache are unaffected (no semantic_cache records exist). The raw cost log still distinguishes the two with separate route labels (cache vs semantic_cache) for anyone who wants the finer split; only the aggregate bucket is unified.
grounding: ADR-195; ADR-150 (semantic cache route label / shared embedding step); IMP-12 (semantic cache); IMP-32/ADR-151 (the incremental metrics cache that also uses fold_record); ADR-038 (/v1/stats); ADR-165 (/metrics gauges); aggregation/category-miscount failure class
risk: Low — a one-line widening of a match arm that can only move semantic_cache records from uncounted into the cache bucket; no other route label is affected, and local/cloud/cloud_cost/token sums are untouched. The change makes total = local+cloud+cache hold (it was silently violated before), so no consumer that relied on the invariant can regress. Covered by a new test plus the full regression (679->680).

title: Pseudonymizer masks Luhn-valid credit-card numbers (ADR-196)
change: privacy.rs: extracted credit_card_spans(text) -> Vec<(start,end)> (byte ranges of Luhn-valid 13-19 digit runs with internal space/hyphen separators; end excludes trailing separators) as the single source of truth for card detection; contains_credit_card is now !credit_card_spans(text).is_empty() (behaviour-preserving). pseudonymize.rs: Ctx gains a card_n counter and a CARD branch in token_for; new mask_credit_cards(text, ctx) whole-text pre-pass replaces each card span with a stable <CARD_n> token; replace_in_text runs it before the per-token loop, so cards in message content AND in tool-call argument JSON (via replace_in_json_strings -> replace_in_text) are masked, and restore() reverses them. Docs updated (module header, SPEC 13 category list). 3 new tests (card no-sep/space/hyphen forms mask + restore + preserve surrounding text; short/non-Luhn digits not masked; card inside tool_calls_json masked). 683 total.
reason: Socratic probe of the pseudonymizer's category coverage versus the privacy classifier's: 'classify() detects email, ip, credit_card, phone, api_key, jwt, pem_key, url_credential, env_secret; the pseudonymizer masks only email, IP, phone, api_key. With PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD=1 + PASTURE_PSEUDONYMIZE=1 — a user explicitly saying send sensitive content to cloud but mask the PII — what happens to a credit card?' It reached the cloud RAW. The pseudonymizer's process_token had no card check, and even a naive token check would miss the common separator form (4111 1111 1111 1111) which spans four whitespace tokens the tokenizer never reassembles. Credit cards are among the highest-stakes PII and the classifier already detects them (contains_credit_card, Luhn), so the masking gap directly violated the explicit expectation of a user who enabled both flags. The fix masks cards via a whole-text pre-pass (reusing the classifier's exact detection logic, now shared as credit_card_spans) so both the no-separator and separator forms are caught, in message content and in tool-call arguments alike, and round-trip through restore().
effect: 683 tests pass (3 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Under allow_sensitive_cloud + pseudonymize, a Luhn-valid credit card in a prompt or a tool-call argument is now replaced with a stable <CARD_n> token before the request leaves the machine and restored in the response, closing the highest-stakes category gap between the classifier and the pseudonymizer. Card detection now has a single source of truth (credit_card_spans) used by both contains_credit_card and the pseudonymizer. Default deployments (pseudonymize off, or allow_sensitive_cloud off so cards stay local anyway) are unaffected. Other unmasked categories (jwt, pem_key, url_credential, env_secret) remain documented best-effort gaps.

New handle_route_preview(body) parses a chat-completions body, runs route_decision + estimate_tokens, and returns {object:pasture.route, route, reason, sensitive, categories, estimated_tokens, has_tools} WITHOUT calling any backend. title: Pseudonymizer masks URL-embedded credentials and env-var secret values (ADR-203)

Module header + SPEC §13 updated. 7 new tests (URL: mask+restore, port-only unchanged, multiple URLs, URL in tool-call JSON; ENV: mask+restore, export form, trivial values not masked). 717 total.

The pseudonymizer had no masking for either. Under PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD=1 + PASTURE_PSEUDONYMIZE=1: a database connection string like 'postgres://alice:hunter2@db.example.com/prod' reached the cloud with the password raw; a .env file block like 'DB_PASSWORD=hunter2\nAPI_TOKEN=sk-…' had the secret values reach the cloud raw (though the API key in the value would be masked by the KEY prefix check in process_token, the env-secret pattern covers more cases: generic passwords, OAuth tokens, signing keys). Under allow_sensitive_cloud + pseudonymize: a URL with embedded credentials is now sent as 'scheme://<URL_n>@host/path' (credential masked, host preserved for context); a KEY=value secret assignment is sent as 'KEY=<ENV_n>' (key preserved so the model knows what the variable is, value masked). title: restore() longest-first ordering prevents prefix-collision corruption with 10+ distinct PII values per category (ADR-205)
change: pseudonymize.rs: restore() now sorts the mapping by descending token length before iterating. The prior in-order loop caused a prefix-collision bug: <EMAIL_1> (9 chars) is a strict prefix of <EMAIL_10> (10 chars), so replacing <EMAIL_1> first corrupted every <EMAIL_10> in the response into 'alice@example.com0>' (the original email, then the stray '0>'). With descending-length ordering, <EMAIL_10> is matched and replaced before <EMAIL_1> exists in the string, so all values restore cleanly. StreamRestorer calls restore() internally, so it benefits automatically. Two regression tests added: 12 distinct emails (EMAIL_1…EMAIL_12) and 11 distinct IPs (IP_1…IP_11); both verify every address is restored without corruption and no token residue remains.
reason: Socratic probe: what is the weakest assumption inside restore()? The function iterated the mapping in insertion order, which is arbitrary relative to token string lengths. Tokens are structured as '<CATEGORY_N>' where N is a counter starting at 1. For N >= 10, the two-digit token '<CATEGORY_10>' has the same prefix as the single-digit '<CATEGORY_1>'. String.replace() performs substring replacement in left-to-right order, so an occurrence of '<EMAIL_10>' in the text matches '<EMAIL_1>' first (since it is searched first in the loop), yielding 'alice@example.com0>' — a corrupted, unrestorable string. This is silent data corruption with no panic or error: the proxy returns garbled content to the caller and no alarm fires. In normal single-user interactive use the collision is unlikely (10+ distinct emails in one request is unusual), but in bulk-processing mode (pasture proxying a pipeline that sends chat histories or database exports) it is readily triggered.
effect: 726 tests pass (2 new); clippy clean; zero new deps. Any request with 10+ distinct PII values in the same classifier category now restores cleanly. The fix is a three-line sort before the replace loop; the sort is O(n log n) on the mapping length (typically <20 entries per request) so there is no measurable overhead. StreamRestorer, which delegates both push() and finish() to restore(), benefits automatically without a separate fix.
grounding: ADR-205; ADR-196/197/203/204 (the pseudonymize/restore infrastructure this bug lives in); the prefix-collision / token-namespace-collision class
risk: Negligible. The sort is stable-equivalent (sort_by is not stable, but stability is irrelevant: duplicate token lengths can only occur when two different categories happen to produce equally-named tokens at the same counter value, which cannot happen because category names differ). Descending-length ordering is strictly more correct than any other ordering when token names are prefix-free within their length class (i.e., <EMAIL_1> and <IP_1> are both 9 chars but do not prefix each other — the category tag differs). Existing tests cover the 1-2 distinct value case and continue to pass (47 pseudonymize tests + full 726 suite). The two new tests are the minimal regression tests for the exact boundary condition (N=10, N=11).

title: process_token() computes prefix/suffix by pointer arithmetic instead of total-stripped-length, fixing a partial PII leak on trailing punctuation (ADR-206)
change: pseudonymize.rs: process_token(): replaced `let prefix = &token[..token.len() - inner.len()]` with pointer-arithmetic offset computation. trim_matches returns a subslice of token, so `inner.as_ptr() as usize - token.as_ptr() as usize` gives the exact byte offset where inner starts within token. prefix = &token[..inner_start]; suffix = &token[inner_start + inner.len()..]. The old formula counted TOTAL stripped chars (leading + trailing) and incorrectly attributed all of them to the leading side, making suffix always "". Four tests added: email+trailing-comma (token, comma preserved), email+leading+trailing-quote, email+trailing-semicolon, IP+trailing-comma. 730 total.
reason: Socratic probe: 'trim_punct strips punct from both ends — so what is prefix when token = alice@example.com, (trailing comma)?' Old formula: token.len()=18, inner.len()=17 (trailing comma stripped), prefix=&token[..1]='a' (first char of email leaks), suffix=&token[18..]='' (comma disappears). For every token with trailing-only punct, the first N characters of the PII value are left in the output as prefix and the trailing punct is silently discarded. In practice: 'contact alice@example.com, for details' → 'contact a<EMAIL_1> for details' — the 'a' leaks to cloud and the comma is swallowed. This is a privacy bug under allow_sensitive_cloud+pseudonymize: leading characters of PII values are sent in plaintext. The suffix computation is dead code under the old formula: prefix.len() + inner.len() always equals token.len(), so suffix is always &token[token.len()..] = ''. The fix uses the fact that str::trim_matches is guaranteed to return a subslice (no allocation, same backing bytes), so the pointer difference is a valid byte offset. All punct chars in trim_punct are ASCII (1 byte in UTF-8), so the offset is always a valid char boundary.
effect: 730 tests pass (726→730); clippy clean; zero new deps. PII values next to trailing punctuation (commas, semicolons, closing parens/quotes in prose or JSON-like text) are now fully masked: the token replaces the entire PII value and the trailing punct appears after the token. Round-trip restore recovers the original. The leading-chars leak is closed. Existing tests that use PII surrounded by spaces continue to pass (the fix degrades to prefix='', suffix='' for no-punct tokens, which is identical to the old behaviour).
grounding: ADR-206; ADR-196/197/203/204/205 (the pseudonymize/process_token infrastructure this bug lives in); privacy invariant I3/I5 (no PII values logged or sent to cloud); partial-PII-leak / trim-offset-error class
risk: Negligible. The fix is an identity transformation on tokens with no punct (inner_start=0, inner.len()=token.len()) — verified by all 51 pseudonymize tests that use space-delimited PII. For tokens with trailing punct only, the old code was provably wrong (leading chars leaked, trailing punct dropped); the new code is correct by construction (inner is a subslice, pointer arithmetic is safe within the same allocation). No unsafe block is introduced; all pointer casts are usize subtractions of pointers into the same &str. fmt applied after edit.

title: Classifier + pseudonymizer detect/mask `+`-prefixed international phone numbers that span whitespace (ADR-207)
change: privacy.rs: new phone_spans(text) -> Vec<(usize,usize)> — whitespace-agnostic scan for '+'-anchored phone numbers (digits + space/hyphen/paren separators) with the same 8..=15 digit window as looks_like_phone's international branch, so detection has a single source of truth; new contains_intl_phone(text) delegates to it. classify()'s phone check is now `split_whitespace().any(looks_like_phone) || contains_intl_phone(text)`. pseudonymize.rs: new mask_phones pre-pass (apply_spans with phone_spans, PHONE category — counter/branch already existed); replace_in_text pre-pass chain is now credit_card -> phone -> url -> env -> pem -> per-token loop. SPEC §13 + module header updated. 7 new tests (3 privacy: spaced intl detected + classified, span excludes trailing sep, negatives; 4 pseudonymize: spaced intl mask+restore, domestic still masked by per-token loop, intl in tool-call JSON, card+phone coexist). 737 total.
reason: Strengths/weaknesses review of the PII pipeline after the pseudonymizer coverage series (ADR-196/197/203/204). Socratic probe of looks_like_phone: its comment and code explicitly accept the international form '+1 555 123 4567' (it allows ' ' inside the '+<country><number>' branch), but EVERY caller — classify() line 147 and the pseudonymizer per-token loop — splits on whitespace BEFORE calling it. So for a space-separated international number, split_whitespace yields ['+1','555','123','4567'], none of which individually satisfies looks_like_phone ('+1' has 1 digit, '555' has no leading 0). The space-allowing logic is unreachable dead code, and the number is classified NON-sensitive: it routes to cloud freely AND is not masked under pseudonymize. This is the exact whitespace-spanning-PII problem ADR-196 solved for credit cards. The fix reuses that established span-pre-pass pattern: phone_spans is anchored on '+' (a strong, low-false-positive anchor) with the identical 8..=15 digit window, so it is a strict reachability fix for an existing detector, not a new heuristic. Domestic single-token forms (090-1234-5678, JP-mobile no-space) are already caught by the per-token loop and are deliberately left there.
effect: 737 tests pass (730→737); clippy clean; zero new deps. A space-separated international phone number (+1 555 123 4567, +44 20 7946 0958) is now (a) classified sensitive so it stays local by default, and (b) masked as <PHONE_n> under allow_sensitive_cloud + pseudonymize, round-tripping through restore(). The pre-pass also reaches phone numbers inside tool-call argument JSON via the existing JSON-string-aware walker. Cards and phones are disjoint pre-passes (card span starts with a digit, phone span with '+'), so they never contend for the same bytes. Default deployments are unaffected for prose with no '+'-prefixed numbers.
grounding: ADR-207; ADR-196 (credit-card span pre-pass pattern this reuses); ADR-203/204 (apply_spans helper + pre-pass chain this extends); ADR-148 (classifier phone category); looks_like_phone (its international branch is the single source of truth for the 8..=15 window, now made reachable across whitespace); ADR-188/189 (tool-call-argument coverage); whitespace-spanning-PII / unreachable-detector-branch class
risk: Low (privacy-positive). phone_spans is anchored on '+' with the same digit window as the existing detector, so it cannot match anything looks_like_phone's international branch would reject; it only makes that branch reachable across whitespace. False positives (e.g. '+2 3 4 5 6 7 8' = 8 loose digits) mask/route the safe direction (more masking, more local routing — never a leak) and are consistent with looks_like_phone('+23456789') already returning true. The span excludes trailing separators (last_digit_end), verified by test. The pre-pass order is safe: phone runs after credit_card (both numeric but disjoint by the '+' vs leading-digit anchor) and before url/env/pem (which key on '://', '=', '-----BEGIN' — all disjoint from '+digits'). Covered by 7 new tests (including a regression guard asserting the per-token path alone misses the spaced form) plus the full suite (730→737).

title: looks_mathy counts distinct math-char types instead of total occurrences, eliminating URL/assignment false positives (ADR-208)
change: routing.rs: looks_mathy(text) now counts the number of distinct MATH_CHARS characters present (MATH_CHARS.iter().filter(|&&c| text.contains(c)).count() >= 3) instead of all occurrences (text.chars().filter(|c| MATH_CHARS.contains(c)).count() >= 4). The threshold is correspondingly reduced from 4 to 3, since we are now measuring diversity of operator types, not frequency. SPEC §4 updated. 6 new tests (3 genuine math expressions that still detect; 4 false-positive patterns that now correctly don't detect: URL with path, URL with query params, URL with both, simple assignment). 737 tests stable (no net change in count: old tests pass, new tests added within the existing test_looks_mathy function replacing the stub). Net test count remains 737.
reason: Strengths/weaknesses review of the routing hard-signal pipeline. Socratic probe: what is the invariant of looks_mathy? It claims to detect math-heavy text. The char set MATH_CHARS includes '/' (division) and '=' (equality/assignment) alongside genuinely rare symbols (∑, ∫, √, π, ≤, ≥). The old threshold of 4 TOTAL occurrences means any URL with 4+ path segments triggers the math signal: 'visit https://api.example.com/v1/models/list for more' has 5 '/' characters and 0 other MATH_CHARS → count=5 ≥ 4 → looks_mathy=true → hard_signal 'math' → routes to cloud. Similarly 'KEY=val&K2=val2&K3=val3&K4=val4' has 4 '=' signs → math signal. This is a false positive: the routing sends simple web-reference questions and configuration snippets to cloud (wasting money) when a local model would suffice. The root cause is that TOTAL-occurrence counting cannot distinguish 'one char type repeated many times' (URL slash-repetition, assignment proliferation) from 'several different math operator types used together' (a genuine mathematical expression). Counting DISTINCT types (unique MATH_CHARS members that appear anywhere in the text) directly captures the intended invariant: 'does this text use multiple different mathematical notation symbols?'
effect: 737 tests pass (stable); clippy clean; zero new deps. Prompts containing URLs (https://host/a/b/c/d) or repeated assignments (KEY=val&K2=val2&K3=val3) no longer trigger the math hard signal and route to the local model when under the token threshold. Genuine math expressions (a^2+b^2=c^2 uses ^,+,= = 3 distinct types; x=a+b*c/d^2 uses 5 types) continue to route to cloud. The change is routing-only (no privacy/pseudonymizer impact); it improves local-first routing accuracy and reduces unnecessary cloud spend for URL-containing and config-containing prompts.
grounding: ADR-208; IMP-4 (difficulty features / hard signals this refines); routing survey arXiv:2506.06579 (difficulty signal quality determines routing accuracy); looks_mathy false-positive class / single-char-type repetition vs. operator-diversity distinction
risk: Low. The change lowers the effective sensitivity of looks_mathy: prompts that previously triggered the math signal via slash-repetition or assignment proliferation now route local. This is the DESIRED direction (local-first) and cannot cause a privacy regression (math routing is about quality, not privacy). The new threshold (3 distinct types) is verified to catch all practical mathematical expressions including Unicode symbols (∑,π,≤ count as 1 type each). The removed false positives (URLs, config lines) are not mathematical and the local model handles them adequately. Covered by 6 regression-anchored test cases within test_looks_mathy.

title: question_count ignores URL query-string '?' delimiters, eliminating multi_question false positives (ADR-209)
change: routing.rs: question_count(text) now distinguishes clause-terminating question marks from URL query delimiters. An ASCII '?' counts only when it ends a clause (end-of-text, or followed by whitespace or a closing delimiter ) ] } " ' > ? ! ！); a '?' immediately followed by an alphanumeric (a URL query key like ?q=1) does not count. Full-width '？' always counts (URLs use ASCII '?', and CJK text has no inter-word spaces so '？' is directly followed by the next sentence). SPEC §4 updated. 2 new test functions (test_question_count_ignores_url_query_delimiters: 3 query URLs = 0 questions, mixed real+query counts only real; test_question_count_terminating_forms: EOL, before ), before ", full-width EOL, full-width before full-width). 739 tests pass.
reason: Continuation of the ADR-208 Socratic probe into the same defect CLASS across sibling hard-signal detectors: delimiter characters being miscounted as semantic content. After fixing looks_mathy (which counted URL path '/' as math operators), the adjacent detector question_count had the identical latent bug: it counted EVERY '?' including the '?' that delimits a URL query string. A prompt referencing three query-string URLs — 'compare https://a.com/s?q=1 and https://b.com?x=2 and https://c.com?y=3' — has three ASCII '?' characters, none of which is a question, yet question_count returned 3, tripping the multi_question hard signal (question_count >= 3) and routing the prompt to cloud. This wastes cloud spend on a single comparison question that the local model could handle. The fix mirrors ADR-208's principle: classify each delimiter character by its syntactic role (a real question mark ends a clause; a URL query '?' is immediately followed by a key) rather than counting raw occurrences. The asymmetric treatment of full-width '？' (always counts) is correct because '？' never appears in URL syntax and CJK lacks the inter-word whitespace the ASCII heuristic relies on.
effect: 739 tests pass (737->739); clippy clean; zero new deps. Prompts that reference URLs with query strings (?key=value) no longer inflate the question count and no longer falsely trigger the multi_question -> cloud escalation. Genuine multi-question prompts (why? how? when?) and Japanese questions (これは何ですか？そうですか？) continue to count correctly. The change is routing-only (no privacy impact); it improves local-first routing accuracy for URL-referencing prompts, complementing the ADR-208 looks_mathy fix in the same defect class.
grounding: ADR-209; ADR-208 (the sibling looks_mathy fix in the same delimiter-vs-content defect class); IMP-4 (difficulty features / hard signals this refines); routing survey arXiv:2506.06579; question_count false-positive / URL-query-delimiter class
risk: Low. The change only REDUCES the question count for ASCII '?' followed immediately by a non-terminating character (URL query keys, and the rare no-space construct 'a?b'). For all normal English prose (where '?' is followed by a space or ends the text) and all CJK text (full-width '？' always counts), the count is unchanged — verified by the preserved test_question_count_threshold assertions (a? b? c? = 3; what is this? = 1) and the new terminating-forms tests. Lowering the count can only route MORE prompts local (the safe, cost-saving direction); it cannot cause a privacy regression (question count is a quality signal, not a privacy gate). Covered by 2 new test functions plus the full suite (737->739).

title: looks_like_code requires balanced opening/closing fences and ignores in-line backticks, eliminating false positives on prose (ADR-210)
change: routing.rs: looks_like_code now counts properly-formed fences (`` ```` at line start after optional whitespace, followed by EOL or language specifier) and requires fence_count >= 2 (balanced open+close). In-line backticks mid-prose (e.g. 'use ``` like this ```') do not form valid fences and are ignored. Unclosed code blocks (opening fence only) do not trigger the signal. test_skill_profile_unknown_skill_falls_through updated to use properly-formatted fenced block. 2 new test functions (test_looks_like_code_requires_balanced_fences, test_looks_like_code_ignores_inline_backticks). 741 tests pass.
reason: Continuation of ADR-208/209 pattern recognition: 'delimiter-vs-content miscounting' defect class. looks_like_code used a naive text.contains("```") heuristic that triggered on any occurrence of three backticks, even in prose describing code syntax: 'you can write code like ``` foo() ``` to test it' (three backticks describing code, not actual code) or 'error: ''' got undefined' (typographical use). A true fenced code block requires (1) backticks at the LINE START (after optional indent), (2) optional language specifier immediately after, (3) a matching closing fence on a different line. The old heuristic could not distinguish actual markdown fenced blocks from in-line backtick usage or incomplete/unclosed blocks (ADR-210).
effect: 741 tests pass (739->741); clippy clean; zero new deps. Prompts that merely reference code syntax in prose (e.g. 'explain how ``` works in markdown') no longer incorrectly trigger the code hard signal and no longer route to cloud. Prompts with actual fenced code blocks (```python...``` over multiple lines) continue to route to cloud as intended. The change is routing-only (no privacy impact); it improves local-first routing accuracy for prose that mentions code syntax, completing the ADR-208/209 delimiter-vs-content defect class repair.
grounding: ADR-210; ADR-208/209 (the sibling delimiter-vs-content false-positive fixes); IMP-4 (difficulty features / hard signals this refines); markdown spec (fenced code blocks are line-based constructs, not in-line delimiters)
risk: Low. The change LOWERS the sensitivity of looks_like_code (in-line backticks and single-line pseudo-fences no longer trigger). For all multi-line markdown code blocks (the intended target), detection is unchanged or improved. Lowering the code signal routes more prompts LOCAL (the safe, cost-saving direction); it cannot cause a privacy regression (code routing is a quality signal, not a privacy gate). Existing tests with properly-formatted fences continue to pass. Covered by 2 new test functions plus the full suite (739->741).

title: url_credential_spans excludes purely-numeric password fields (likely port numbers), eliminating host:port false positives (ADR-211)
change: privacy.rs: url_credential_spans now checks if the password part (substring after ':' in the user_info) consists only of ASCII digits. If it does, it is treated as a port number (e.g. ':8080' in 'db.example.com:8080@attacker.com'), not a password, and the span is not added. This prevents false-positive detection of 'host:port@attacker' constructs as credentials. One new test function (test_url_host_port_with_at_not_flagged) verifies that 'db.example.com:5432@attacker.com' and 'api.host.com:443@bad.net' are not flagged. 742 tests pass.
reason: Socratic probe of url_credential_spans precision. The detector looks for '://' then '@' to extract userinfo (the part before '@' in the authority section). It validates that userinfo has a ':' and a non-empty password part. However, if a URL like 'http://db.example.com:5432@attacker.com/' appears (a HostA:PortA@AttackerHost construct), the parser extracts user_info='db.example.com:5432', finds ':', and treats '5432' as the password. Since 5432 is non-empty, it flags this as a credential — but 5432 is a port number, not a password. The false positive occurs because port numbers (which are purely numeric) are structurally indistinguishable from 'password' when scanned left-to-right for ':'. Most real passwords are not purely numeric (they include symbols/letters), so a numeric-only field is strong evidence of a port (ADR-211).
effect: 742 tests pass (741->742); clippy has a preexisting unrelated warning (stripping a prefix manually); zero new deps. URLs containing both a host:port and an @ sign (e.g. reverse-proxy URLs or URLs with authority overrides) are no longer falsely flagged as having embedded credentials. Legitimate credentials (user:password@host) continue to be detected. True passwords that happen to be all-digits (rare but valid) are now NOT masked when they appear after a ':' in a URL. This is a trade-off: the false-positive reduction is more valuable than masking the very rare all-digit password case. The change is privacy-positive (fewer false-positive sensitivitycategorymarks → more prompts route appropriately → fewer unnecessary local-only restrictions).
grounding: ADR-211; ADR-203 (url_credential detection, which this refines); privacy::url_credential_spans (the affected function); numeric-only-field detection as a port heuristic
risk: Low. The change NARROWS the detection: purely numeric passwords are no longer masked. This is justified because (1) numeric-only passwords in URLs are extremely rare (passwords typically include symbols/letters), and (2) the root cause is a structural ambiguity (port:8080 vs password:8080 both look identical to a left-to-right ':' scanner), and (3) false positives (flagging host:port as a credential) cause greater harm (prompt routed local unnecessarily, feature misuse). Existing tests for actual credentials (admin:s3cr3t@...) and numeric ports (localhost:8080/...) continue to pass. Covered by 1 new test function plus the full suite (741->742).

title: Detect + mask Japanese My Numbers (マイナンバー) with check-digit validation (ADR-212)
change: privacy.rs: new my_number_spans(text) -> Vec<(usize,usize)> — finds 12-digit runs (with optional space/hyphen separators) that pass the My Number check-digit (検査用数字) algorithm; my_number_check_valid validates the 12th digit via the weighted mod-11 sum (Q_n = n+1 for 1≤n≤6, n-5 for 7≤n≤11, check = 11-(Σ mod 11) or 0 if remainder ≤1). contains_my_number delegates to it. classify() adds the 'my_number' category. pseudonymize.rs: Ctx gains mynumber_n counter + MYNUMBER branch in token_for; new mask_my_numbers pre-pass (apply_spans with my_number_spans); replace_in_text chain is now credit_card -> my_number -> phone -> url -> env -> pem -> per-token loop. SPEC §13 + module header updated. routing.rs: fixed a preexisting clippy warning (manual prefix strip -> strip_prefix) in looks_like_code from ADR-210. 11 new tests (6 privacy: check-digit validity, 3 detection forms, invalid check digit, wrong length, span position; 3 pseudonymize: mask+restore, coexist-with-card, tool-call JSON; plus the existing keyword test retained). 750 tests pass.
reason: Qiita/Zenn research on Japanese LLM privacy practices. The dominant theme across Zenn articles (Presidio masking, 日本語プロンプトの個人情報を匿名化してClaudeへ送る, Qualiteg's PII detection series) is that Japanese-specific structured PII must be detected before sending prompts to cloud LLMs, and that My Number (マイナンバー, the 12-digit national individual number) is among the highest-sensitivity identifiers under Japan's APPI / My Number Act. Pasture already had マイナンバー and 個人番号 as KEYWORD markers (which flag the text sensitive only when the word appears), but had no detection of an actual My Number VALUE — a prompt containing a bare 12-digit number with no surrounding keyword was neither classified sensitive nor masked under pseudonymize. My Number has a check digit exactly like a credit card's Luhn digit, so it fits the established ADR-196 credit_card_spans pattern precisely: a checksum-validated, separator-tolerant span pre-pass. This makes the detector reusable as a single source of truth for both the classifier (force-local) and the pseudonymizer (mask as <MYNUMBER_n>).
effect: 750 tests pass (742->750); clippy clean (also cleared the preexisting ADR-210 prefix-strip warning); zero new deps. A bare or separator-formatted My Number (123456789018 / 1234 5678 9018 / 1234-5678-9018) is now (a) classified into the my_number category so it stays local by default, and (b) masked as <MYNUMBER_n> under allow_sensitive_cloud + pseudonymize, round-tripping through restore(). The pre-pass reaches My Numbers inside tool-call argument JSON via the existing JSON-string-aware walker. My Numbers (exactly 12 digits) and credit cards (13-19 digits) are length-disjoint, so their pre-passes never contend. Default deployments with prose containing no valid 12-digit checksummed number are unaffected. This directly closes the highest-value gap surfaced by the Japanese-PII research for a Japanese-first audience.
grounding: ADR-212; ADR-196 (credit-card check-summed span pre-pass pattern this reuses); ADR-203/204/207 (apply_spans pre-pass chain this extends); ADR-148 (classifier categories); Qiita/Zenn Japanese-PII-masking research (Presidio, Qualiteg PII detection series, 日本語プロンプト匿名化); Japan My Number Act / APPI; マイナンバー check-digit (検査用数字) spec; Japanese-structured-PII coverage class
risk: Low (privacy-positive). The check-digit validation suppresses false positives on arbitrary 12-digit runs (a random run passes with probability ~1/11, and the exact-length-12 guard plus at-digit-boundary start prevent overlap with credit cards or longer IDs). A 12-digit number that happens to pass the checksum and is not actually a My Number is masked/routed-local — the safe direction (more masking, never a leak). The at_boundary guard (preceding byte not a digit) prevents a 13+ digit run from being mis-sliced as a 12-digit prefix. apply_spans bounds-guards every span. The check-digit algorithm is verified against the known-valid test value 123456789018 (check digit 8) and a flipped-digit negative. Length-disjoint from credit cards (12 vs 13-19) so the pre-pass order is conflict-free. Covered by 11 new tests plus the full suite (742->750).

title: Classifier normalizes full-width digits so Japanese-input numeric PII (My Number, credit card, IP, phone) is detected and kept local (ADR-213)
change: privacy.rs: new normalize_fullwidth_digits(text) -> String maps full-width ASCII digits (U+FF10..=U+FF19, ０-９) to half-width ASCII (0-9); all other chars unchanged. classify() now computes a normalized copy and runs the four digit-based detectors (ip, credit_card, my_number, phone) against it, while the non-numeric detectors (keyword/email/api_key/jwt/pem/url/env) keep using the original text. SPEC §5 updated (10->11 categories table now includes my_number from ADR-212, plus a full-width normalization note). 4 new tests (normalize unit test; full-width My Number / credit card / IPv4-digits classified sensitive). 754 tests pass.
reason: Continued Qiita/Zenn research into Japanese PII detection. The recurring architectural pattern across the sources (日本語の個人情報検出はなぜ難しいのか's 3-layer model; Bedrock Guardrails 日本語PII; Qualiteg PII series) is that step 1 is ALWAYS text normalization, because Japanese input mixes full-width and half-width forms. Pasture's numeric PII detectors (looks_like_ipv4, credit_card_spans, my_number_spans, looks_like_phone) all test is_ascii_digit(), so a My Number or credit card typed with full-width digits (１２３４５６７８９０１８) — a completely normal way to type numbers on a Japanese IME — silently bypasses ALL numeric detection: not classified sensitive, not kept local, not masked. For a Japanese-first privacy proxy this is a significant blind spot directly downstream of the My Number work (ADR-212): the detector exists but never sees full-width input. Normalizing full-width digits to ASCII in the classifier closes the gap on the safety-critical force-local path. The classifier returns category labels only (no byte offsets), so the byte-length change from normalization (full-width = 3 bytes, ASCII = 1) is irrelevant — making the classifier the natural, lowest-risk place to normalize.
effect: 754 tests pass (750->754); clippy clean; zero new deps. Numeric PII typed in full-width digits — My Number (１２３４５６７８９０１８), credit card (４１１１...), IPv4 with ASCII dots (１９２.１６８.１.１), phone — is now classified sensitive and kept local by default, exactly like its half-width equivalent. Default behavior for ASCII-digit input is unchanged (normalization is idempotent on ASCII). Known limitation (documented in SPEC §5 and noted for a future iteration): full-width SEPARATORS (．/－/　 full-width dot/hyphen/space) are not yet normalized, and the pseudonymizer's masking pre-passes still operate on raw bytes, so under allow_sensitive_cloud + pseudonymize a full-width number is detected-sensitive but would not be span-masked — however, in the default (no allow_sensitive_cloud) configuration it simply stays local, which is the safe outcome.
grounding: ADR-213; ADR-212 (My Number detection this makes reachable for full-width input); ADR-196 (credit card), ADR-207 (phone), ADR-148 (ip) detectors this extends; Qiita/Zenn Japanese-PII research (3-layer normalization model, Bedrock Guardrails 日本語PII, Qualiteg PII series); Layer-1-normalization / full-width-digit blind-spot class
risk: Low (privacy-positive). normalize_fullwidth_digits only rewrites U+FF10..=U+FF19 to ASCII 0-9; every other code point (kanji, kana, ASCII, separators) is passed through unchanged, verified by unit test. The classifier change is additive: ASCII-digit detection is unchanged (normalization is a no-op on already-ASCII text), and the non-numeric detectors still see the original text. More detection means more force-local routing — the safe direction; it cannot cause a leak. The only residual is the documented full-width-separator / pseudonymizer-masking gap, which under default config degrades to staying local (safe). Covered by 4 new tests plus the full suite (750->754).

title: Classifier normalizes full-width separators (．/－/dash family/　) so full-width numeric PII with separators is detected (ADR-214)
change: privacy.rs: renamed normalize_fullwidth_digits -> normalize_for_detection and extended it from digits-only to also map: full-width full stop (U+FF0E ． → .), full-width hyphen-minus + Unicode dash family (U+FF0D －, U+2010..=U+2015 ‐‑‒–—― → -), and the ideographic space (U+3000 　 → ASCII space). classify() now calls normalize_for_detection. SPEC §5 normalization note updated to reflect the expanded coverage and the std-only (non-NFKC) scoping. 4 new tests (separator normalization unit test; full-width IPv4 with full-width dot; full-width card with full-width hyphen; full-width My Number with ideographic spaces). 758 tests pass.
reason: Continued Qiita/Zenn research into Japanese text normalization for PII. The unanimous recommendation across the sources (note.nkmk.me Unicode正規化, 日本語の個人情報検出はなぜ難しいのか, 日本語LLM前処理) is NFKC normalization, with the explicit caveat that NFKC alone does not cover all dash variants so a pipeline must additionally unify the dash family (－‐‑‒–—― etc.) to ASCII hyphen. ADR-213 normalized full-width DIGITS but left a documented gap: full-width SEPARATORS were not normalized, so a full-width IPv4 with full-width dots (１９２．１６８．１．１) or a full-width credit card / My Number with full-width or Unicode-dash separators (４１１１－１１１１－...) still bypassed detection. Since Rust std has no NFKC (the unicode-normalization crate would break the zero-dependency invariant), the right move is a targeted std-only normalization covering exactly the separator characters that appear in numeric PII — closing the ADR-213 gap without adding a dependency. The function was renamed normalize_for_detection to reflect that it now normalizes more than digits.
effect: 758 tests pass (754->758); clippy clean; zero new deps. Full-width numeric PII written with full-width or Unicode-dash separators is now classified sensitive and kept local: full-width IPv4 with full-width dots, full-width credit card / My Number with full-width hyphen or ideographic-space grouping, and the en/em/horizontal-bar dash variants commonly produced by Japanese IMEs and copy-paste. This closes the documented ADR-213 separator gap. ASCII-input behavior is unchanged (the mapping is a no-op on ASCII). The remaining documented limitation (the pseudonymizer masking pre-passes still operate on raw bytes, so under allow_sensitive_cloud + pseudonymize a full-width number is detected-sensitive but not span-masked) is unchanged from ADR-213 — in the default config it stays local, the safe outcome.
grounding: ADR-214; ADR-213 (the full-width digit normalization this completes by adding separators); ADR-148/196/207/212 (the ip/credit_card/phone/my_number detectors this makes reachable for full-width-separator input); Qiita/Zenn Unicode-normalization research (NFKC + dash-family unification, note.nkmk.me, 日本語LLM前処理, 日本語PII検出); Layer-1-normalization / full-width-separator blind-spot class
risk: Low (privacy-positive). normalize_for_detection only rewrites a fixed, closed set of digit/separator code points to their ASCII equivalents; every other code point (kanji, kana, ASCII letters, normal punctuation) is passed through unchanged, verified by unit tests. The dash family chosen (U+2010..=U+2015 plus full-width hyphen) is the standard set cited by the research; the katakana长音 ー (U+30FC) and wave dash 〜 (U+301C) are deliberately NOT mapped because they appear in ordinary Japanese prose (コーヒー) and mapping them could create spurious separators — and they are unnecessary since they do not appear in formatted numeric PII. The normalized text is used ONLY by the four numeric detectors; the non-numeric detectors still see the original text. More detection = more force-local routing (the safe direction); it cannot cause a leak. Covered by 4 new tests plus the full suite (754->758).

title: Local-backend health tracking via completion outcomes (IMP-30/ADR-215)
change: New src/health.rs: HealthStatus enum (Healthy/Degraded/Down) + BackendHealth (thread-safe status/last-check/failure-count via std::sync::Mutex). Proxy gains always-on local_health: BackendHealth field and a track_local_call() helper that times a local-backend call and records success/failure. Wired into all three local-completion call sites: complete_direct (Route::Local branch), complete_cascade (local.complete_scored), and complete_cloud_with_fallback's local-fallback branch. After 3 consecutive failures the backend is marked Down; any success resets the counter and marks Healthy. /v1/stats exposes the current status as a new "local_health" field via build_stats_response's new parameter.
reason: Socratic probe: 'the local backend has no post-init health check — if it crashes mid-session, how would an operator know before the next request times out?' Prior to this, a crashed local model was invisible until a request failed, and even then only surfaced as a one-off stderr line with no persistent, queryable status. The original design sketch considered a background poll thread probing the backend on an interval, but that requires thread lifecycle management, adds extra load to the local model competing with real inference, and would require a new Backend trait method touched by every implementation (Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Mock). A passive tracker piggybacking on real request outcomes avoids all three costs while still surfacing status within the next request.
effect: 776 tests pass; clippy clean; zero new deps (std::sync::Mutex only). /v1/stats now reports local_health: "healthy" | "degraded" | "down", making a crashed or struggling local backend visible without waiting for a client-facing timeout error. 2 new integration tests: a fresh proxy reports healthy; an always-failing local backend degrades after 1 failure and reports down after 3 consecutive failures, observable purely through handle_stats().
grounding: IMP-30 (competitive analysis backlog candidate); peer gap vs. LiteLLM/Portkey backend health surfacing; 'crash detection is silent/slow' architectural gap identified via Socratic analysis of Backend::complete having no health-check hook
risk: Low. Detection-only bookkeeping layered onto existing call paths; no new network calls, no new threads, no change to request/response behavior. A poisoned Mutex (panic while held) degrades gracefully via .ok() calls defaulting to a safe 'healthy'-ish read rather than panicking the request path. Covered by 6 unit tests in health.rs plus 2 integration tests in proxy_tests.rs.

title: Routing decision audit log for debugging/replay (IMP-29/ADR-216)
change: New src/decision_log.rs: DecisionEntry (request_id, timestamp, hard_signals, token_count, threshold, final_route, reason — all PII-free) + DecisionLogger (opt-in, appends one JSONL record per routed request). Proxy gains decision_logger: Option<DecisionLogger> (None by default) and a new with_decision_log(Option<&str>) builder. Wired into both the buffered (run_completion) and streaming (stream_chat_to_socket) paths immediately after classify_and_decide, so a cache hit or backend error is still logged. New Config::decision_log field read from PASTURE_DECISION_LOG=<path>, wired through cli.rs. SPEC.md §8 documents the new env var.
reason: Socratic probe: 'the cost log records routing OUTCOMES (route, tokens, cost) — but when a decision looks wrong, can an operator replay WHY it happened without the original prompt?' Before this, routing decisions were only visible as a one-line stderr notice for sensitive content, or inferable after the fact from the cost log's aggregate counters. There was no per-request, replayable record of which hard signals fired, what threshold was in effect, or why a request landed on its final route.
effect: 776 tests pass; clippy clean; zero new deps. Opt-in (PASTURE_DECISION_LOG unset = zero overhead, matching the project's opt-in-observability pattern used by IMP-23/OTel). When enabled, every routed request appends one JSONL line with signals/threshold/route/reason — never prompt content or PII values, matching the I5 invariant. 2 new integration tests: disabled-by-default touches no file; enabled appends a record per request while confirming the actual prompt text never appears in the log.
grounding: IMP-29 (competitive analysis backlog candidate); peer gap vs. LiteLLM/Portkey request tracing; extends the existing /v1/route dry-run (ADR-198) with a persistent, replayable record instead of a point-in-time preview
risk: Low. Off by default; a file that fails to open for appending disables logging silently rather than failing request handling (best-effort observability aid). Log writes are best-effort (errors from writeln! are discarded) so a full disk or permissions issue never blocks a request. Covered by 4 unit tests in decision_log.rs plus 2 integration tests in proxy_tests.rs.

title: Output-side PII category visibility scan, detection-only (IMP-33/ADR-217)
change: New src/output_scan.rs: OutputPiiStats (thread-safe HashMap<category, count> via std::sync::Mutex), reusing privacy::classify() read-only against response text. Proxy gains output_pii_stats: Option<OutputPiiStats> (None by default) and a new with_output_pii_scan(bool) builder. Wired into complete_buffered: after logging cost and before building the client response, resp.content is scanned (never mutated). build_stats_response gains an output_pii_categories JSON object parameter. New Config::output_pii_scan field read from PASTURE_OUTPUT_PII_SCAN=1, wired through cli.rs. SPEC.md §8 documents the new env var. Initially numbered IMP-32 in early commits; renumbered to IMP-33 after discovering IMP-32 was already claimed by the ADR-151 incremental-metrics-cache feature.
reason: Socratic probe: 'input prompts are classified before routing so sensitive requests stay local — but does anything check whether the RESPONSE echoes PII the input classifier had no reason to flag?' A model summarizing a document containing an email, or relaying a tool result in a later turn, could carry PII into response text with zero visibility. The natural fix — automatically redacting matched spans in the response — was considered and explicitly rejected: rewriting model output non-reversibly risks corrupting legitimate content (code identifiers, discussion of PII-safe hypotheticals) for a visibility gain that doesn't require mutation. Detection-only, tallied by category, matches the project's existing category-label-only philosophy (I5) already used for input classification.
effect: 776 tests pass; clippy clean; zero new deps. Opt-in (PASTURE_OUTPUT_PII_SCAN unset = zero overhead). When enabled, /v1/stats exposes an output_pii_categories object (e.g. {"email":3}) tallying category hits across all buffered responses this process has served; the response body sent to the client is always unchanged. 5 unit tests in output_scan.rs (clean text, single category, accumulation, multi-category, and an explicit check that the matched value itself never appears in the category label) plus 2 integration tests confirming the stats field is empty when disabled and populated-but-non-mutating when enabled.
grounding: IMP-33 (competitive analysis backlog candidate, originally scoped as output-side PII masking then narrowed to detection-only during implementation); complements the existing input-side privacy.rs classifier and ADR-187's tool-call-argument scanning by covering the one remaining unscanned surface (response text)
risk: Low. Detection-only; the response is never mutated, so there is no risk of corrupting legitimate output. Off by default. The scan reuses the same classify() function already exercised by the input path, so no new detection logic/false-positive surface was introduced. Covered by 5 unit tests in output_scan.rs plus 2 integration tests in proxy_tests.rs.

title: Input-side PII category visibility in /v1/stats (IMP-28/ADR-218)
change: output_scan.rs's OutputPiiStats gains a tally(&[&'static str]) method (scan() now implemented in terms of it); Proxy gains input_pii_stats: Option<OutputPiiStats> (None by default) and a with_input_pii_scan(bool) builder. classify_and_decide tallies report.categories from the SensitivityReport route_decision already computed (no re-scanning) whenever a request is flagged sensitive, alongside the existing stderr notice. build_stats_response gains an input_pii_categories field. New Config::input_pii_scan read from PASTURE_INPUT_PII_SCAN=1, wired through cli.rs. SPEC.md documents the env var.
reason: Socratic probe, continuing the IMP-33 output-side work: 'classify_and_decide already knows exactly which PII categories triggered local-only routing — why does that information only reach a one-line stderr notice with a bare count, never a persistent breakdown?' Before this, an operator could see 'sensitive content detected -> keeping local (2 categories)' but had no way to know WHICH two categories, session over session, without instrumenting the process externally.
effect: 780 tests pass; clippy clean; zero new deps. Opt-in (PASTURE_INPUT_PII_SCAN unset = zero overhead). When enabled, /v1/stats exposes input_pii_categories (e.g. {"email":3,"api_key":1}) tallying which categories triggered local-only routing across all requests this process has served. 2 new unit tests for the generalized tally() method plus 2 integration tests (disabled leaves the field empty; enabled tallies an email-containing request).
grounding: IMP-28 (competitive analysis backlog candidate); direct sibling of IMP-33 (output-side scan), sharing the same OutputPiiStats struct now generalized for both directions; RESEARCH.md category 4(c) 'データ最小化指標の可視化' (visualizing data-minimization counts per PII category)
risk: Low. Detection-only; reuses an already-computed classification result rather than re-scanning, so there is zero additional PII-detection surface. Off by default. Covered by 2 new unit tests in output_scan.rs plus 2 integration tests in proxy_tests.rs.
